children.translated_text: The <s>Tattvayāthārthyadīpana</s> (Illumination of the True Meaning of the Principles), composed by <s>Bhāvāgaṇeśa</s>, son of <s>Śrī Bhāvā Viśvanātha Dīkṣita</s>.

<s>Tattvayāthārthyadīpana</s>.
Composed by <s>Śrī Bhāvāgaṇeśa</s>.
Salutation to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra</s>.

children.text: puruṣaḥ sa jayatyādyaḥ sā ca prakṛtirīśvarī /
children.translated_text: Victorious is that primordial <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), and she, <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the sovereign Goddess,
by whom, having united, endless crores of universes (<s>brahmāṇḍas</s>) are created. (1)
I bow to the teachers <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Āsuri</s>, and <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and to the excellent master of knowledge (<s>Vijñānācārya</s>),
for the growth of intellect or for the accomplishment of all undertakings. (2)
Relying upon the <s>Samāsasūtras</s> (the Sāṃkhya aphorisms in summary) and the commentary of <s>Pañcaśikha</s>,
<s>Bhāvāgaṇeśa</s> composes the <s>Tattvayāthārthyadīpana</s>. (3)

children.text:
tatra tāvadviviktapuruṣajñānaṃ mokṣasādhanamiti |
yebhyo vivektavyo yaśca vivecanīyaḥ tadubhayaṃ sūtratrayeṇoddiśati |
children.translated_text: Now, the knowledge of the isolated <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit) is the means to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). The three <s>sūtras</s> indicate both that from which [the <s>Puruṣa</s>] is to be distinguished and that which is to be discerned:
[The eight <s>Prakṛtis</s> (productive principles). (Tats. 1)]

children.text:
prakarṣeṇa kurvantīti prakṛtayaḥ |
tattvāntarārambhakatvaṃ prakṛtitvamiti sāmānyalakṣaṇam |
tāśca avyaktabuddhyahaṃkārapañcatanmātrarūpāḥ |
tatrāvyaktaṃ nityaṃ śabdādiguṇaśūnyaṃ sattvādiguṇatrayaṃ ca |
sāmyāvasthopalakṣitā guṇāḥ prakṛtirityekaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca |
akāryā guṇā ityaparam |
tathā prakṛtiparyāyā avyaktaṃ pradhānaṃ brahma akṣaraṃ kṣetraṃ tamaḥ māyā brāhmī vidyā avidyā prakṛtiḥ śaktiḥ ajā ityādayaḥ |
sattvādiguṇavatī sattvādyatiriktā prakṛtiriti tu na śaṅkanīyam |
kintu guṇa eva prakṛtiḥ |
sattvādīnāmataddharmatvaṃ tadrūpatvāditi sāṃkhyapravacanasūtreṇa sattvādīnāṃ prakṛtisvarūpatvahetunā prakṛtidharmatvapratiṣedhāt |
prakṛterguṇa ityādivākyaṃ tu vanasya vṛkṣā itivad boddhavyam |
"sattvaṃ rajastama iti prakṛterabhavan guṇā" iti prakṛtikāryatvavacanaṃ tu guṇanityatāvākyavirodhena mahattattvakāraṇībhūtakāryasattvādiparameva |
mahadādisṛṣṭirhi guṇavaiṣamyācchrūyate tacca vaiṣamyaṃ sajātīyasaṃvalanena prakāśādiphalopahitaḥ sattvādivyavahārayogyaḥ kāraṇaguṇānāṃ pariṇāma iti |
etenāṣṭāviṃśatitattvapakṣo 'pyupapādito mantavyaḥ |
sattvāditrayaṃ aha dravyatve 'pi puruṣopakaraṇatvād guṇā ityucyante |
dravyatvaṃ caiṣāṃ saṃyogavibhāgādimattayā upādānakāraṇatvena siddham |
eṣāṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvapravādastu dharmadharmyabhedāt |
manasaḥ saṃkalpātmakatvavat |
tāni ca sattvādīni pratyekaṃ saṃkhyāvyaktikāni laghutvādidharmairanyonyaṃ sādharmyaṃ vaidharmyaṃ ca guṇānāmiti sāṃkhyapravacanasūtrāt |
atra hi sūtraṃ laghutvādinā bahūnāṃ sattvānāṃ sādharmyaṃ tenaiva rajastamobhyāṃ vaidharmyam |
evaṃ ca laghutvādinā bahūnāṃ rajasāṃ gurutvādinā bahūnāṃ tamasāṃ sādharmyavaidharmye ukte iti |
teṣu tritvavacanaṃ tu sattvatvādivibhājakopādhitrayeṇaiva vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ navadravyavacanavaditi |
tāni ca sattvādīni yathopayogamaṇuvibhuparimāṇakāni |
madhyamaparimāṇatve 'nityatvāpattiḥ |
sarveṣāṃ vibhutve kāryāṇāṃ paricchinnatvānupapattiḥ |
ākāśaprakṛtervibhutvasyaivaucityāt |
nanu prakṛteścāparicchinnatvaikatvākriyatvamiti sāṃkhyasiddhāntaḥ |
sa ca virudhyata iti cet maivam gandhasya pṛthivīvyāpakatvavatprakṛtervyāpakatvam |
tacca prakṛtitvasya daiśikābhāvapratiyogitānavacchedakatvam |
ekatvaṃ ca sargabhedena nānātvābhāvaḥ |

children.translated_text: Actionlessness means the absence of the specific activities of determination, self-assertion, and the like.
Otherwise, the agitation of <s>Prakṛti</s> established in <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) would be inexplicable.

children.text: prakṛtyanumānaṃ cetthaṃ mahadādikāryaṃ pakṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakadravyakāryamiti sādhyaṃ kāryatve sati sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvāditi hetuḥ vastrādikāryaśayyāsanavaditi dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: The inference of <s>Prakṛti</s> is as follows: the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is that <s>Mahat</s> and the other effects exist; the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) is that they are effects of a substance whose nature is pleasure, pain, and delusion; the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is that they are effects possessing the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion; the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is like cloth and other effects, and beds, seats, and the like.
<s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> are supporting evidences, and reasoning [is auxiliary to them].

They are called <s>Prakṛtis</s> because they produce (<s>prakarṣeṇa kurvanti</s>) eminently. The general definition of being a <s>Prakṛti</s> is the capacity to initiate another principle (<s>tattva</s>). These are of the form of <s>Avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). Among these, the <s>Avyakta</s> is eternal, devoid of qualities such as sound, and possesses the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s>. One definition is: the <s>guṇas</s> characterized by the state of equilibrium are <s>Prakṛti</s>. Another is: the <s>guṇas</s> are uncaused. The synonyms of <s>Prakṛti</s> are: <s>Avyakta</s> (unmanifest), <s>Pradhāna</s> (primary matter), <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Akṣara</s> (imperishable), <s>Kṣetra</s> (field), <s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Śakti</s> (power), <s>Ajā</s> (unborn), and so on. One should not doubt that <s>Prakṛti</s> possesses <s>Sattva</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s> and is something distinct from them; rather, the <s>guṇas</s> themselves are <s>Prakṛti</s>. Because the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacanasūtra</s> denies that <s>Sattva</s> and the others have the properties of <s>Prakṛti</s>, since their non-possession-of-its-properties is due to their being its very form. The statement '<s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s>' should be understood like 'trees of the forest.' The statement that '<s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> are <s>guṇas</s> produced from <s>Prakṛti</s>' refers specifically to the <s>Sattva</s> and the others that are effects serving as the cause of <s>Mahat</s> (the great principle), due to the contradiction with the statement of the eternity of the <s>guṇas</s>. For the creation of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest is heard to arise from the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, and that disequilibrium is a transformation of the causal <s>guṇas</s> through homogeneous intermixture, endowed with the results of illumination and the like, and fit for the designation of <s>Sattva</s> and the rest. By this, the doctrine of twenty-eight principles is also to be considered established. The three — <s>Sattva</s> and the rest — though they are substances, are called <s>guṇas</s> because they serve the <s>Puruṣa</s>. Their substantiality is established by their possessing conjunction, disjunction, and the like, and by being material causes. The statement that they have the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion is due to the non-difference of attribute and attribute-bearer, just as mind is said to have the nature of deliberation. And those <s>Sattva</s> and the rest are individually manifold in number, with mutual similarity and dissimilarity among the <s>guṇas</s> through properties such as lightness — according to the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacanasūtra</s>. For the <s>sūtra</s> states that many <s>Sattvas</s> have mutual similarity through lightness and the like, and dissimilarity from <s>Rajas</s> and <s>Tamas</s> through the same. And similarly, the mutual similarity of the many <s>Rajases</s> through lightness and the like, and of the many <s>Tamases</s> through heaviness and the like, and their dissimilarity are stated. The use of the term 'three' (for the <s>guṇas</s>) is by the three distinguishing conditions of <s>Sattva</s>-hood and the rest, just as the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> speak of nine substances. Those <s>Sattva</s> and the rest are of atomic, all-pervading, or finite size as needed. If they were of medium size, impermanence would follow. If all were all-pervading, the finite nature of effects would be inexplicable. Since all-pervasiveness is appropriate only for space and <s>Prakṛti</s>. Now, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine holds that <s>Prakṛti</s> is unlimited, one, and actionless. If it is objected that this contradicts [evidence], this is not so — <s>Prakṛti</s>'s pervasiveness is like the pervasiveness of smell in earth. And that [pervasiveness] is the non-limitation of <s>Prakṛti</s>-hood by spatial absence. Oneness means the absence of multiplicity distinct from the distinctions of creation.

children.text: nanu sukhasyāntarevānubhavāt śayyāsanādau sukhe kiṃ pramāṇaṃ yena dṛṣṭāntatā syāditi cenna kāraṇaguṇā hi kāryaguṇānārabhante iti nyāyena viṣayeṣu triguṇakāryeṣu sukhaduḥkhamohasiddheḥ ghaṭarūpamiti pratyayavat candanasukhaṃ strīsukhamityādisukhapratyayādapi viṣaye sukhādyucitaṃ sukhaduḥkhotpādakatvācca tadgatameva sukhaduḥkhādikaṃ sidhyati antaḥkaraṇasukhādihetutayā 'pi viṣaye sukhādikaṃ siddhyati |
children.translated_text: Now, if it is objected that pleasure is experienced only internally, and what is the evidence for pleasure in beds, seats, and the like, so that they could serve as examples — this is not so. Because by the principle that the qualities of the cause produce the qualities of the effect, pleasure, pain, and delusion are established in objects which are effects of the three <s>guṇas</s>. Just as there is the cognition 'the color of the pot,' so also from cognitions such as 'the pleasure of sandalwood' and 'the pleasure of a woman,' pleasure and the rest are properly attributed to the object. And since objects produce pleasure and pain, pleasure, pain, and the rest are established as belonging to them. Even as causes of pleasure and the rest in the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), pleasure and the rest are established in the objects.

children.text: kālādibhedairekasyā eva tryādivyakteḥ sukhaduḥkhotpādakatvācca tadgatameva sukhaduḥkhādikaṃ siddhyati ||
children.translated_text: And because a single entity with three or more manifestations produces pleasure and pain through differences of time and other conditions, pleasure, pain, and the rest are established as belonging to it.
Thus concludes the examination of the root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).

children.text:
atha buddhirnirūpyate |
triguṇātmakamādyaṃ kāryaṃ buddhirityekaṃ lakṣaṇam |
niścayavṛttikamantaḥkaraṇaṃ buddhiriti dvitīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
tasyā dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryākhyaprakṛṣṭaguṇayogāt mahatsañjñā tadapi tṛtīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
tasyāḥ paryāyāḥ |
mano matirmahān brahmā pūrvaṃ buddhirvṛttiḥ khyātiḥ prajñā santatiḥ smṛtiriti |
children.translated_text: Now <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is examined. One definition: <s>Buddhi</s> is the first effect, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>. Second definition: <s>Buddhi</s> is the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) whose function is determination. Third definition: it is called <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) because of its connection with the excellent qualities called <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty). Its synonyms: <s>Manas</s> (mind), <s>Mati</s> (thought), <s>Mahān</s> (the Great), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Pūrva</s> (the Prior), <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Vṛtti</s> (activity), <s>Khyāti</s> (discernment), <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>Santati</s> (continuity), <s>Smṛti</s> (memory).
And in the <s>Anusmṛti</s>:
'<s>Mahān</s>, <s>Ātmā</s>, <s>Mati</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, and the Valorous One,

children.text: buddhiḥ prajñopalabdhiśca tathā brahmā vṛttiḥ smṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Upalabdhi</s>, and likewise <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vṛtti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s> —
by these synonymous terms, the Great Self (<s>Mahān Ātmā</s>) is designated.'
'With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere,

children.text: sarvataḥ śrutimāṃlloke sarvaṃ vyāpya sa tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: with hearing everywhere in the world, it stands pervading all.'
'Those who are wise, free from greed, and who have conquered anger,

children.text:
vimuktāḥ sarva evaite mahattvamupayāntyuta /
  viṣṇurevādisargeṣu svayambhūrbhavati prabhuḥ // iti /
children.translated_text:
all those who are liberated indeed attain Greatness (<s>Mahattva</s>).
<s>Viṣṇu</s> himself becomes the self-born lord in the primordial creations.'

children.text:
idameva mahattattvamaṃśato rajastamaḥsambhedena pariṇataṃ sat vyaṣṭijīvānāmupādhiradharmādiyutaṃ kṣudramapi bhavati |
mahaduparāgādviparītamiti sāṃkhyapravacanasūtrāt |
mahadahaṃkāramanastritayātmakasyāntaḥkaraṇavṛkṣasya mahattattvamaṅkurāvastheti |
atra prakṛtermahānityādisṛṣṭikrame śāstrameva pramāṇam |
idameva mahattattvaṃ kāryeśvarasya svayambhuva upādhistenaivopādhinā sa sarvajñaḥ sarveśvaraḥ sarvakarttā sarvapālakaḥ sarvasaṃharttā ca |
children.translated_text: This very <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is the limiting adjunct of the Lord of Effects (<s>Kāryeśvara</s>), the Self-Born (<s>Svayambhū</s>). Through that very adjunct he is omniscient, the lord of all, the creator of all, the protector of all, and the destroyer of all.
In the <s>Mātsya</s> [Purāṇa]:
'From the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primary matter) with its modifications, the <s>Mahat-tattva</s> was born;
since from it the designation 'Great' always arises for the worlds.'

This very <s>Mahat-tattva</s> (Great Principle), when partially transformed through admixture of <s>Rajas</s> and <s>Tamas</s>, becomes the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of individual souls (<s>vyaṣṭi-jīvas</s>), endowed with <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) and the like, and becomes diminished. This follows from the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacanasūtra</s>: 'from the <s>Mahat</s>'s coloring, the opposite [occurs].' The <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is like the sprout-stage of the tree of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), which consists of the triad of <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>Manas</s>. Here, in the order of creation — 'from <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Mahān</s>' and so forth — scripture alone is the authority.

children.text:
guṇebhyaḥ kṣobhamāṇebhyastrayo devā vijajñire /
  ekā mūrttistrayo devā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ // iti /
children.translated_text:
'From the <s>guṇas</s> being agitated, three gods were born;
one form, three gods — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.'

children.text:
sa ca svayambhūḥ kriyāśaktimat kevalamahattattvopādhikaḥ sūtrātmetyucyate |
sa evārddhasuṣuptāvarddhalayāt prājña ityucyate |
samagrasuṣuptau tu samagralayena nirviśeṣacinmātrasvarūpeṇāvasthānādīśvara ityucyate śrutismṛtipurāṇeṣu mahāṃstridhā taduktaṃ vaiṣṇave |
children.translated_text: That Self-Born One, possessing the power of action, conditioned by the pure <s>Mahat-tattva</s> alone, is called <s>Sūtrātman</s> (the Thread-Self). He himself, in the state of half-deep-sleep and half-dissolution, is called <s>Prājña</s> (the Wise One). In complete deep sleep, due to complete dissolution, he abides in the form of undifferentiated pure consciousness and is called <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). In <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and <s>Purāṇas</s>, the Great One is [described as] threefold. As stated in the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [text]:

children.text:
sāttviko rājasaścaiva tāmasaśca tridhā mahāniti |
brahmaśaṅkaropakṣayāpyādau viṣṇurevāvirbhavatītyardhenoktam |
pūrvoktadharmādiṣu dharmeṇordhvagamanamūrdhvagamanena bhogasthānānyupalakṣyante |
tena pātālabhūsvargādīnāmapi saṃgrahaḥ |
jñānena mokṣaḥ vairāgyeṇa prakṛtilayaḥ puruṣatattvānabhijñasya vairāgyāt prakṛtilayo bhavati |
tathā coktaṃ purāṇe |
children.translated_text: 'The Great is threefold: <s>sāttvika</s> (of <s>Sattva</s>), <s>rājasa</s> (of <s>Rajas</s>), and <s>tāmasa</s> (of <s>Tamas</s>).' And it is half-stated that even when <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s> are present, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone manifests first. Among the aforementioned <s>dharma</s> and the rest: through <s>dharma</s> there is upward movement; by upward movement, the realms of enjoyment are indicated — thereby <s>Pātāla</s>, earth, heaven, and the rest are all included. Through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), there is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). Through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), there is dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> — for one who is unacquainted with the <s>Puruṣa</s> principle, dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> occurs through dispassion. As stated in the <s>Purāṇa</s>:

children.text:
prakṛticintakānadhikṛtya "pūrṇaṃ śatasahasraṃ tu tiṣṭhanti vigatajvarā" iti |
atra prakṛtigrahaṇena mahadahaṃkārabhūtendriyāṇyapi gṛhyante |
tatra vairāgyapūrvakaṃ teṣu teṣvātmabhāvenopāsyamāneṣu layo hi prakṛtāviti ca śrūyate |
children.translated_text: Among these, when each is meditated upon with dispassion as the self, 'dissolution indeed occurs in <s>Prakṛti</s>' — thus it is heard [in scripture].
Immediately after the preceding statement:
'The contemplators of the sense organs dwell for ten <s>Manvantaras</s>;
the contemplators of the elements for a full hundred; those of the <s>Abhimānika</s> (ego-derived) for a thousand;

Regarding the contemplators of <s>Prakṛti</s>: 'They dwell for a full hundred thousand [years], free from affliction.' Here, by the term '<s>Prakṛti</s>,' <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, the elements, and the sense organs are also included.

children.text: bauddhā daśa sahasrāṇi tiṣṭhanti vigatajvarāḥ // iti ca /
ayaṃ ca prākṛtiko bandha ityucyate yogibhiḥ mahadādibhāvaśca vaikṛtiko bandha iti |
children.translated_text: And this is called by the <s>yogins</s> the natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>) bondage, while the state of <s>mahat</s> and other [evolutes] is the derived (<s>vaikṛtika</s>) bondage.
Non-obstruction through sovereignty — sovereignty refers to the <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) such as <s>aṇimā</s> and others.
Thus <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) has been explained.
the contemplators of <s>Buddhi</s> dwell for ten thousand, free from affliction.'

children.text:
ahaṅkāro vyākhyāyate |
mahattattvādahaṅkāra utpadyate aṅkurācchākhāvat |
tasya cāhamākāravṛttimattvādahaṅkāra iti saṃjñā |
ahaṃvṛttimadantaḥkaraṇamahaṅkāra ityekaṃ lakṣaṇam |
ekādaśendriyopādānatvaṃ dvitīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
tanmātropādānatvaṃ tṛtīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
tasya ca paryāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) is now explained. From <s>mahat-tattva</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> arises, like a branch from a sprout. And because it possesses the modification of 'I'-ness (<s>aham-ākāra-vṛtti</s>), it is called <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. The inner instrument having the modification of 'I'-ness is <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — this is one definition. Being the material cause of the eleven sense-organs is [another] definition.

children.text:
ahaṅkāro 'bhimānaśca karttā mantā ca sa smṛtaḥ /
  ātmā ca prakulo jīvo yataḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ // iti /
children.translated_text: <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> is also known as self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>), the doer (<s>kartā</s>), the thinker (<s>mantā</s>); it is remembered as the self (<s>ātmā</s>), the primal one (<s>prakula</s>), the living being (<s>jīva</s>) — from which all activities [arise].
And this <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is of three kinds.
Thus it is said in the <s>Kūrma</s> [Purāṇa]:
<s>Vaikārika</s> (sattvic), <s>taijasa</s> (rajasic), and <s>bhūtādi</s> which is <s>tāmasa</s> (tamasic) —
this threefold <s>ahaṅkāra</s> arose from <s>mahat</s>.
And [these are] the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specifics) as stated in the <s>Kūrma</s> [Purāṇa].
From the <s>taijasa</s> [ahaṅkāra] the sense-organs arise; the ten <s>devas</s> (presiding deities) are from the <s>vaikārika</s>;
and the eleventh, the mind (<s>manas</s>), by its own quality is of both natures.

children.text:
bhūtatanmātrasargastu bhūtāderabhavat prajā // iti /
vaikārikaḥ sāttvikastaijaso rājasaḥ |
svaguṇena sarvendriyeṣu sāhāyyarūpeṇotkarṣeṇobhayātmakaṃ jñānakarmendriyobhayātmakamityarthaḥ |
indriyadevatāśca digvātārkapracetośvivahnīndropendramitrakāmacandraśceti ekādaśa |
children.translated_text: The creation of <s>bhūta-tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) arose from <s>bhūtādi</s> [ahaṅkāra]. <s>Vaikārika</s> is <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>taijasa</s> is <s>rājasa</s>. 'By its own quality, being of both natures' means — in all the sense-organs, in the form of assistance through its superior quality, it is of both natures, i.e., of the nature of both knowledge-organs and action-organs. The presiding deities of the sense-organs
Thus ends the exposition of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>.

children.text:
atha tanmātrā ucyante |
śabdasparśarūparasagandhā nirviśeṣāstadvanti sūkṣmabhūtāni tanmātrāḥ |
nirviśeṣaśabdādiguṇavad dravyaṃ tanmātrā iti sāmānyalakṣaṇam |
ahaṃkāropādānatve sati tattvāntarārambhakatvaṃ dvitīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
tattannirviśeṣaguṇavattvaṃ tattanmātralakṣaṇam |
tāni ca pañca śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātraṃ ceti |
śāntaghoramūḍhāḥ pañcasvapi viśeṣāḥ śabdatvasparśatvādivyāpyā jātiviśeṣā eva |
śabde tu udāttānudāttasvaritāḥ niṣādarṣabhagāndhāraṣaḍjamadhyamadhaivatāḥ pañcamaśceti svarāḥ |
sparśe śītoṣṇatve |
rūpe śuklatvādayo viśeṣāḥ |
te ca śvetapītaraktaśyāmaharitakapiśāḥ |
rase madhuratvādayo viśeṣāste ca madhuratiktakaṣāyakaṭvamlakṣārāḥ ṣaḍrasāḥ |
children.translated_text: In taste, the specifics are sweetness and so forth — sweet, bitter, astringent, pungent, sour, and salty — the six tastes.
In smell, [the specifics are] fragrant and non-fragrant.
Devoid of these specifics, possessing those [general qualities], substances are <s>tanmātras</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ paryāyāḥ tanmātrāṇi tamovigrahāḥ sūkṣmavigrahāḥ sūkṣmabhūtāni aviśeṣā iti //
children.translated_text: Their synonyms are: <s>tanmātrāṇi</s>, bodies of darkness (<s>tamo-vigrahāḥ</s>), subtle bodies (<s>sūkṣma-vigrahāḥ</s>), subtle elements (<s>sūkṣma-bhūtāni</s>), and non-specifics (<s>aviśeṣāḥ</s>).

Now the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are described. Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — non-specific, possessing those [qualities], subtle elements — [these are] the <s>tanmātras</s>. A substance having non-specific qualities of sound, etc. is a <s>tanmātra</s> — this is the general definition. Being the effect of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and being the initial cause of other <s>tattvas</s>,
Thus [there are] five <s>tanmātras</s>.
Thus the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (root-natures) have been explained.
[The sixteen <s>vikāras</s> (modifications). <s>Tattva-sūtra</s> 2.]

children.text:
ṣoḍaśa vikārā iti dvitīyaṃ sūtram |
ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtāni ca ete ṣoḍaśa vikārāḥ |
tatra śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇāni svasvaviṣayakabuddhijanakatvāt pañca buddhīndriyāṇi |
vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāni svasvakarmakaraṇāt pañca karmendriyāṇi |
tatra uccāraṇaṃ vācaḥ hastayorādānaṃ pādayorgatiḥ pāyorutsargaḥ upasthasyānandaḥ |
sarvasahāyatvādubhayātmakaṃ manaḥ |
etānyekādaśendriyāṇi |

children.translated_text: being the effect of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and not being the cause of any other <s>tattva</s> — this is one definition.
Being the effect of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, being conjoined with the body, being an instrument of action, being supersensuous — [such] is an <s>indriya</s> (sense-organ) — this is the second [definition].

children.text: atha paryāyāḥ indriyāṇi karaṇāni nipātanāni vaikārikāṇi taijasāni |
children.translated_text: Now the synonyms: <s>indriyāṇi</s> (sense-organs), <s>karaṇāni</s> (instruments), <s>nipātanāni</s>, <s>vaikārikāṇi</s> (from <s>vaikārika</s>), <s>taijasāni</s> (from <s>taijasa</s>).
Thus ends the exposition of the sense-organs (<s>indriyas</s>).

'Sixteen modifications' — this is the second <s>sūtra</s>. The eleven sense-organs and the five gross elements — these are the sixteen modifications. Among them, hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell — being the producers of cognition regarding their respective objects — are the five organs of knowledge (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>). Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals

children.text:
atha mahābhūtāni |
pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśamiti |
saviśeṣaśabdādimattvaṃ mahābhūtatvamityekaṃ lakṣaṇam |
tattvāntarānārambhakatve satyārambhakatvaṃ dvitīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
saviśeṣaśabdaguṇavattvamākāśasya lakṣaṇam |
saviśeṣaśabdasparśavattvaṃ vāyorlakṣaṇam |
saviśeṣaśabdasparśarūpavattvaṃ tejasaḥ |
saviśeṣaśabdasparśarūparasavattvamapām |
saviśeṣaśabdasparśarūparasagandhavattvaṃ pṛthivyāḥ |
etāni viśeṣalakṣaṇāni |
etāni pañca mahābhūtāni parasparopakārīṇi |
athāmīṣāṃ paryāyāḥ |
bhūtāni vikārā viśeṣā ākṛtayaḥ tamovigrahāḥ śāntā ghorā mūḍhā iti |
children.translated_text: Now the gross elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>): earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), water (<s>ap</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), wind (<s>vāyu</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>). Having specific qualities of sound, etc. constitutes being a gross element — this is one definition. Being an effect and not being the cause of any other <s>tattva</s> — this is the second definition. Having the specific quality of sound constitutes the definition of space.
Thus the sixteen modifications have been explained.
[<s>Puruṣa</s>. <s>Tattva-sūtra</s> 3.]

children.text:
puruṣa iti tṛtīyaṃ sūtram |
anādiḥ sūkṣmaścetanaḥ sarvagataḥ nirguṇaḥ kūṭastho nityo draṣṭā bhoktā kṣetravit amanaḥ prasavadharmā ceti svarūpam |
kūṭasthanitya ityekaṃ lakṣaṇam |
mukhyabhoktṛtvamityaparaṃ lakṣaṇam |
vṛttisākṣitvamiti tṛtīyaṃ lakṣaṇam |
atha paryāyāḥ puruṣa ātmā pumān pudgalajantuḥ jīvaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ naraḥ kaviḥ brahma akṣaraḥ prāṇaḥ jñaḥ yaḥ kaḥ sa eka iti |

children.translated_text: Thus these are the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>; from the knowledge of these, one becomes accomplished (<s>kṛtakṛtya</s>).
And thus the authoritative statement of <s>Pañcaśikha</s>:
One who knows the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, in whichever stage of life (<s>āśrama</s>) he may dwell,

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vā 'pi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: whether with matted hair, shaved head, or wearing a topknot — he is liberated; of this there is no doubt.

'<s>Puruṣa</s>' — this is the third <s>sūtra</s>. Beginningless, subtle, conscious, all-pervading, without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>), eternal, the witness (<s>draṣṭā</s>), the experiencer (<s>bhoktā</s>), the knower of the field (<s>kṣetravit</s>), without mind, and of the nature of creation — [such is] its essential nature. Being immutable and eternal is one definition. Being the primary experiencer is another.

children.text:
sa ca puruṣo nānā sukhaduḥkhamohajanmamaraṇabandhamokṣavyavasthātaḥ janmādivyavasthātaḥ puruṣabahutvamiti sāṃkhyapravacanasūtrāt |
yadyekaḥ puruṣaḥ syādekasmin sukhite sarve sukhitāḥ syuḥ evaṃ sarvatra evaṃ puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham |
evaṃ tāvat sāṃkhyācāryāḥ kapilāsuripañcaśikhapatañjaliprabhṛtayo yasmāt paraṃ nāparamasti kiñciditi nyāyavaiśeṣikāśca bahūn puruṣānātmatvena vadanti |
aupaniṣadāścācāryā hariharahiraṇyagarbhavyāsādayaḥ ebhyo 'tiriktamekameva nityeśvaraṃ sarveṣāmātmānaṃ vadanti |
kasmādevaṃ puruṣa evedaṃ sarvamiti |
tadevāgnistadāditya iti |
tadakṣaraṃ tadvibhurvareṇyaṃ yasmāt paraṃ nāparamasti kiñcit sa hi sarveṣu bhūteṣu sthāvareṣu careṣu ca vasatyeko mahānātmā yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
children.translated_text: And that <s>Puruṣa</s> is many — from the differences of pleasure, pain, delusion, birth, death, bondage, and liberation — [this follows] from the <s>Sāṃkhya-pravacana-sūtra</s>: 'the multiplicity of <s>puruṣas</s> [is established] from the differences of birth, etc.' If there were only one <s>puruṣa</s>, when one is happy, all would be happy; likewise everywhere.
In a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in worms and insects, in a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, in a cow, in an elephant,
in cattle, gadflies, and mosquitoes — the wise see the [same] form.

children.text: ekameva yathā sūtraṃ suvarṇe varttate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a single thread runs through
gold, pearls, jewels, corals, clay, and silver —
so in cattle and humans, likewise in elephants, deer, and others,
this one Self (<s>ātman</s>) should be known as established everywhere.

children.text:
ityādi pramāṇebhyaḥ |
sāṃkhyāstu ādipuruṣaviṣayatayā layāvaśiṣṭanirviśeṣacinmātraviṣayatayā vā etāni śrutivākyāni yojayanti |
children.translated_text: From such authoritative statements and others. But the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> interpret these Vedic (<s>śruti</s>) statements as pertaining to the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, or as pertaining to the undifferentiated pure consciousness that remains after dissolution (<s>laya</s>).
Thus ends the exposition of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Thus the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> have been explained.

children.text:
sāṃkhyakārikā ca |
  mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtirmahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta /
  ṣoḍaśakastu vikāro na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ // iti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> [states]: 'Root <s>Prakṛti</s> is uncreated; <s>mahat</s> and the other seven are both <s>prakṛtis</s> (sources) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (modifications); the group of sixteen are only modifications; <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>.'

children.text: idānīṃ prathamasūtreṇaiva guṇātmakaprakṛteruddiṣṭatve 'pi guṇānāmavāntaravibhāgaṃ taddharmāṃśca vivecayituṃ vakṣyamāṇasañcarapratisañcaropodghātasaṅgatyā ca sūtraṃ pravarttate |
children.translated_text: Now, although <s>Prakṛti</s> constituted by the <s>guṇas</s> has been indicated by the first <s>sūtra</s> itself, in order to distinguish the subdivisions of the <s>guṇas</s> and their properties, and in connection with the introduction to the forthcoming [topics of] <s>sañcara</s> (evolution) and <s>pratisañcara</s> (involution), the [next] <s>sūtra</s> is set forth.
[The three <s>guṇas</s> (<s>traiguṇya</s>). <s>Tattva-sūtra</s> 4.]

children.text:
traiguṇyamiti caturthaṃ sūtram |
sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ teṣāṃ samāhārastriguṇaṃ triguṇameva traiguṇyam |
tatra sattvaṃ nāma prakāśalāghavaprasannatābhiṣvaṅgaprītititikṣādilakṣaṇamanantabhedaṃ samāsataḥ sukhātmakam |
rajo nāma śokatāpasvedastambhodvegonmādādilakṣaṇamanantabhedaṃ samāsato duḥkhātmakam |
tamo nāma adānāpuṇyadainyagauravālasyanidrāpramādādilakṣaṇamanantabhedaṃ samāsato mohātmakam |
eteṣāṃ lakṣaṇāni |
children.translated_text: 'The three <s>guṇas</s>' — this is the fourth <s>sūtra</s>. <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are the three <s>guṇas</s>; their aggregate is <s>triguṇa</s>; <s>triguṇa</s> itself is <s>traiguṇya</s> (the triplicity of qualities). Among them, <s>sattva</s> is characterized by illumination, lightness, serenity, attachment, joy, endurance, and so forth — of infinite varieties.
<s>Sattva</s> should be known as illuminating; <s>rajas</s> should be known as activating;
<s>tamas</s> should be known as having the nature of inertia (<s>laya</s>) — this is called <s>traiguṇya</s> (the triplicity of qualities).
These three <s>guṇas</s> are the causes of origination, maintenance, and dissolution of all [things].
Thus <s>traiguṇya</s> (the triplicity of qualities) has been explained.

children.text: idānīṃ saguṇanirguṇaśrutiviṣayopapattyarthaṃ sargādāvutpannaṃ svayambhuvaṃ pralayāvaśiṣṭanirviśeṣacitsāmānyaṃ ca darśayituṃ sṛṣṭipralayayoḥ sūtradvayaṃ pravartate |
children.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of establishing the consistency of the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural) passages regarding <s>saguṇa</s> (with attributes) and <s>nirguṇa</s> (without attributes), and to show <s>Svayambhū</s> (the Self-born) who arises at the beginning of creation and the undifferentiated general consciousness (<s>nirviśeṣacitsāmānya</s>) that remains after dissolution, two <s>sūtras</s> concerning creation and dissolution are presented.
[<s>Saṃcara</s> (Creation). || Tats_5 ||]
[<s>Pratisaṃcara</s> (Dissolution). || Tats_6 ||]

children.text:
sañcaraḥ pratisañcaraḥ |
sañcaraḥ sṛṣṭiḥ pratisañcaraḥ pralayaḥ |
tatra sṛṣṭiryathā |
avyaktākhyā prakṛtiḥ pravṛttisvabhāvā svatantrā ca |
sargādau svayameva kṣubdhā satī bhāvinārāyaṇabījabhūtā pūrvakalpe svayambhūpālakena nāmakena vyaktena nārāyaṇapuruṣeṇa saṃyujyate tataśca sajātīyairanyaiḥ prakṛtyaṃśairnyūnādhikabhāvena militā satī cetanācetanātmakaṃ mahattattvamārabhate |
nanu puruṣasya prakṛtisaṃyogitve asaṃyogo hyayaṃ puruṣa iti śrutivirodha iti cenna vikārahetusaṃyogasyaiva saṅgaśabdārthatvāt anyathā śrutismṛtiṣu jalasaṃyogino 'pi padmapattrasyāsaṅgatādṛṣṭāntatā na syāt |
tatra mahattattvasya svarūpeṇa mukhyotpattiḥ cetanasya tu abhivyaktirūpā kāryatā |
yogabhāṣye vyāsadhṛtavākyānnavadhā kāryatā |
children.translated_text:
<s>Saṃcara</s> and <s>Pratisaṃcara</s>.
<s>Saṃcara</s> means creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>); <s>Pratisaṃcara</s> means dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>).
As for creation: <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), called <s>Avyakta</s> (the Unmanifest), whose nature is activity and who is independent, at the beginning of creation, being agitated of its own accord and serving as the seed of the future <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, becomes conjoined with the manifest <s>Puruṣa</s> (Spirit) named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the protector <s>Svayambhū</s> of the previous <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle). Then, being combined with other portions of <s>Prakṛti</s> of the same class in varying proportions, it produces the <s>Mahattattva</s> (Great Principle), which is both conscious and unconscious.
Now, if <s>Puruṣa</s>'s conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s> is objected to on the grounds that the <s>śruti</s> says 'this <s>Puruṣa</s> is indeed unattached' — that is not so, because the word 'attachment' (<s>saṅga</s>) refers only to conjunction that is the cause of modification; otherwise, the illustration of the lotus leaf, which is in contact with water yet unattached, used in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, would not apply.
Therein, the <s>Mahattattva</s> has a primary origination in its own form, while for the conscious principle the causation is in the form of manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>).
According to the statement cited by <s>Vyāsa</s> in the <s>Yogabhāṣya</s>, causation is of nine kinds:

"Origination, persistence, manifestation, modification, obtaining a condition,
separation, alteration, and sustenance — causation is remembered as ninefold."

children.text:
evamādiśaktirapi cetanaviśeṣo mahattattvakāraṇībhūtaguṇatrayasambandhāt svayambhavāpyādāvutpadyate |
utpattau ca pramāṇaṃ prayogasāre |
children.translated_text:
Thus <s>Ādiśakti</s> (the Primordial Power) too, being a special form of consciousness, arises at the very beginning even from <s>Svayambhū</s>, due to her connection with the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) that have become the cause of <s>Mahattattva</s>.
The authority for this origination is in the <s>Prayogasāra</s>:
"Therefore she came forth, eternal, all-pervading, born of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."

children.text:
vāyavīyasaṃhitāyāṃ ca /
  śivecchayā parā śaktiḥ śivatattvaikatāṃ gatā /
  tataḥ parisphuratyādau sarge tailaṃ tilādiva // iti /
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Vāyavīya Saṃhitā</s>:
"By the will of <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme <s>Śakti</s> (power), having attained oneness with the <s>Śiva</s> principle,
then manifests at the beginning of creation, like oil from sesame seeds."
And in the <s>Pañcarātra</s>:
"Thus beholding that <s>Śakti</s>, whose form is existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>),
whose form is the superintendence of the effulgence of the synthesis of all principles,

children.text: vyaktāṃ karoti nityāṃ tāṃ prakṛtiṃ paramaḥ pumān // iti /

children.translated_text: "There appeared the Mother of the Universe, the Mother of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
the <s>Śakti</s> consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, designated <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> (Root Nature)."
the Supreme Person makes manifest that eternal <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)."

children.text:
tasyāmahaṃ samutpannastattvaistairmahadādibhirityādiśivavākyācca |
saiva prakṛtyadhiṣṭhātrī devatā mahālakṣmī ambā bhavānī haimavatī durgā ityādipadairabhilapyate purāṇādiṣu |
saiva ca līlāvigrahairādipuruṣeṇa militā satī sṛṣṭiṃ pālayati |
taduktaṃ śaṅkarācāryaiḥ |
children.translated_text:
"From her arose <s>Ahaṃ</s> (the I-principle), with those <s>tattvas</s> (principles) such as <s>Mahat</s> and the rest" — and from the statement of <s>Śiva</s> and the like.
That same deity who superintends <s>Prakṛti</s> is referred to in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and elsewhere by the terms <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, <s>Ambā</s>, <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, and so on.
And she, united with the Primordial Person through her playful forms (<s>līlāvigraha</s>), sustains the creation.
As stated by <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>:

children.text:
śivaḥ śaktyā yukto yadi bhavati śaktaḥ prabhavituṃ
  na cedevaṃ devo na khalu kuśalaḥ spanditumapi / iti /
children.translated_text:
"If <s>Śiva</s> is united with <s>Śakti</s>, he is able to create;
otherwise, the god is not even capable of stirring."

children.text:
evaṃ sarvatattvānāṃ tattaddevatānāṃ ca sahaivotpattirjñeyā |
utpattikramastu nirūpaṇakrameṇaiva |
etasmānmahato guṇāntarasaṃvalitāt trividho 'haṅkāra utpadyate cetanācetanātmakaḥ vaikāriko rājasastāmasaśceti |
tataścāhaṅkārāt saṅkalpapūrvakaṃ dehendriyāṇi pañca tanmātrāṇi cotpadyante |
svayabhuva indriyāṇi devatārūpāṇi vaikārikāt vyaṣṭīndriyāṇi ca taijasāt teṣvindriyeṣvādau mana utpadyate |
children.translated_text:
Thus it should be known that all <s>tattvas</s> (principles) and their respective deities arise simultaneously.
The order of their origination, however, follows the order of exposition.
From this <s>Mahat</s>, combined with other <s>guṇas</s>, the threefold <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle) arises, both conscious and unconscious: <s>Vaikārika</s> (modified), <s>Rājasa</s> (passionate), and <s>Tāmasa</s> (dark).
Then from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, with deliberation, the five bodily senses and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) arise.
The sense-organs of <s>Svayambhū</s>, in the form of deities, arise from the <s>Vaikārika</s>, and the individual sense-organs from the <s>Taijasa</s>. Among those sense-organs, <s>Manas</s> (mind) arises first.
"From the desire for sound, the ear arises for this one whose self is purified;
from the desire for form, the eye; the nose from the desire to grasp smell;"

children.text:
ityādinā mokṣadharmādau śrotrādīnāṃ manovṛttirāgādikāryatvaśravaṇāt |
indriyatanmātrayośca kāryakaraṇabhāvasyābhāvāt kramaniyamo nāsti |
tatrendriyeṣu nāstyavāntarakāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ pramāṇābhāvāt |
tanmātreṣu tvasti sa yathā ahaṃkārācchabdatanmātraṃ tasmādahaṃkārotpannācchabdatanmātrādahaṃkārasahitāt sparśatanmātraṃ śabdasparśobhayaguṇakam |
evaṃ krameṇaikaikaguṇavṛddhyā tanmātratrayamutpadyate |
tataśca tanmātrebhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtāni jāyante |
tatrāhaṅkārāt pañcatanmātrāṇāṃ taddvārā pañcamahābhūtānāṃ cotpattau purāṇe krama uktaḥ sa yathā
children.translated_text:
and so on — because in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> and elsewhere it is heard that the hearing organ and the others are effects of mental desires such as passion.
Since there is no cause-effect relationship between the sense-organs and the <s>tanmātras</s>, there is no fixed order.
Among the sense-organs, there is no intermediate cause-effect relationship, due to the absence of evidence.
But among the <s>tanmātras</s>, there is such a relationship: from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> arises the <s>śabdatanmātra</s> (sound-subtle element); from that <s>śabdatanmātra</s>, which has arisen from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, together with <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, arises the <s>sparśatanmātra</s> (touch-subtle element), possessing the two qualities of sound and touch.
Thus, by successive increase of one quality each, three more <s>tanmātras</s> arise.
Then from the <s>tanmātras</s>, the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) are born.
Regarding the origination of the five <s>tanmātras</s> from <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, and through them the five <s>mahābhūtas</s>, the sequence is stated in the <s>Purāṇa</s> as follows:
"<s>Bhūtādi</s> (the Elemental Principle), undergoing transformation, created the <s>śabdamātra</s> (sound-element).
<s>Ākāśa</s> (space), hollow, arose from it, characterized by sound.
<s>Ākāśa</s>, undergoing transformation, created the <s>sparśamātra</s> (touch-element).

children.text: vāyurutpadyate tasmāt tasya sparśo guṇo mataḥ //
children.translated_text: From that, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) arises; its quality is considered to be touch."

children.text:
ityādikrameṇeti |
nanvevamākāśādibhūtacatuṣṭayasyāpi tattvāntaraprakṛtyāpattyā kevalavikṛtitvāṣṭaprakṛtitvasiddhāntakṣatiriti cenna ākāśādīnāṃ sparśāditanmātreṣvahaṃkāropaṣṭambhamātreṇa kāraṇatvasya purāṇeṣūktatvāditi |
evaṃ trayoviṃśatitattvānāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ |
teṣu pañcamahābhūtāni varjjayitvā 'haṃkāraṃ ca buddhau praveśya saptadaśakaṃ liṅgaśarīrasañjñaṃ bhavati |
vahnerindhanavadātmano 'bhivyaktisthānatvāt |
tacca sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ svasvabījabhūtaprakṛtisaṃyogāt sargādāvutpadya prākṛtapralayaparyantaṃ tiṣṭhati |
tenaiva cehalokaparalokayorjīvānāṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ bhavati |
prāṇaśca buddhereva vṛttibheda ityato liṅaśarīre pṛthak na nirdiśyate buddhāvevāntarbhāvāt |
tasya ca liṅgaśarīrasya paramasūkṣmāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni tejaḥpradhānānyāśrayaḥ citrādivat āśrayaṃ vinā lokāntaragamanāsambhavāt |
taduktaṃ saptatyām |
children.translated_text:
And so on in this sequence.
Now, if it is objected that the four elements beginning with <s>Ākāśa</s>, being also modifications of other principles, would compromise the doctrine of eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (original principles) by reducing them to mere modifications — that is not so, because in the <s>Purāṇas</s> it is stated that <s>Ākāśa</s> and the rest serve as causes for the <s>tanmātras</s> of touch and so on only through the support of <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>.
Thus the creation of the twenty-three <s>tattvas</s> is explained.
Among these, excluding the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> and subsuming <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> under <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), the group of seventeen is called the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body),
because it is the locus of manifestation for the <s>ātman</s> (self), like fuel for fire.
This subtle body, for all <s>puruṣas</s> (souls), arises at the beginning of creation through the conjunction of <s>Prakṛti</s> as its own seed, and persists until the cosmic dissolution (<s>prākṛtapralaya</s>).
By it alone occurs the transmigration (<s>saṃsaraṇa</s>) of souls in this world and the next.
<s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is merely a function of <s>Buddhi</s>; therefore it is not separately enumerated in the subtle body, being included within <s>Buddhi</s>.
The support of that subtle body consists of the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> in their most subtle form, with fire predominating, like a painting — because transmigration to other worlds would be impossible without a support.
As stated in the <s>Saptati</s> (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s>):

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayamṛte sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā chāyā /
children.translated_text: "Just as a painting does not stand without a support, just as a shadow does not exist without posts and the like,

children.text: tadvadvinā viśeṣairna tiṣṭhati nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam // iti
children.translated_text: so too the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand without a support, without the specific elements."

children.text:
idaṃ ca liṅgaśarīramādau svayambhuvaḥ samaṣṭicetanasya upādhibhūtamekameva samaṣṭirūpaṃ jāyate tataśca vyaṣṭijīvānāmapyupādhibhūtāni vyaṣṭiliṅgaśarīrāṇi tadaṃśabhūtāni tato vibhajyante piturliṅgaśarīrāt puttraliṅgaśarīravat |
taduktaṃ sāṃkhyapravacanasūtreṇa |
vyaktibhedaḥ karmaviśeṣāditi |
manunā 'pyuktam |
children.translated_text:
This subtle body, at the beginning, is the single aggregate form that serves as the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of <s>Svayambhū</s>, the aggregate consciousness. Then from it, the individual subtle bodies that serve as limiting adjuncts for individual souls are separated as its portions — like a son's subtle body from a father's subtle body.
As stated by the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana Sūtra</s>:
"The differentiation of individuals is due to the specificity of <s>karma</s>."
And as stated by <s>Manu</s>:

children.text:
teṣāṃ tvavayavān sūkṣmān ṣaṇṇāmapyamitaujasām /
  sanniveśyātmamātrāsu sarvabhūtāni nirmame // iti /
children.translated_text:
"Combining the subtle particles of those six, each of immeasurable power,
with the individual souls, he created all beings."

children.text:
ṣaṇṇāmiti ṣaḍindriyaṃ samastaliṅgaśarīropalakṣakam |
tathā cāyamarthaḥ |
svayambhūḥ svaliṅgaśarīrāvayavān sūkṣmānalpān ātmamātrāsu svāṃśacetaneṣu saṃyojya sarvaprāṇinaḥ sasarjeti |
children.translated_text:
"Of those six" — the six sense-organs serve to indicate the entire subtle body.
Thus the meaning is: <s>Svayambhū</s>, having joined the subtle, minute portions of his own subtle body with the individual conscious beings who are his own portions, created all living beings.
Thus the exposition of the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body).

children.text:
atha sthūlaśarīrotpattiḥ |
daśaguṇitamahattattvamadhye 'haṃkārastasminnapi daśaguṇe vyoma tathaiva vyomnyapi vāyuḥ vāyāvapi tejaḥ tejasi daśaguṇe jalaṃ tathaiva jalasyāpi daśaguṇasya madhye pṛthvī samutpadyate saiva sthūlaśarīrasya bījamaṇḍarūpeṇa pariṇamate |
tasyāpi daśaguṇitasyāṇḍasya pṛthivyāvaraṇasya madhye caturdaśabhuvanātmakaṃ svayambhuvaḥ sthūlaśarīraṃ tatsaṅkalpādevotpadyate |
tenaiva śarīreṇa svayambhūrnārāyaṇa ityucyate |
svayambhuvaṃ prakṛtya manunā 'pyuktam |
children.translated_text:
Now, the origination of the gross body (<s>sthūlaśarīra</s>).
Within the <s>Mahattattva</s> multiplied tenfold, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> arises; within that, tenfold again, <s>Ākāśa</s> (space); likewise within <s>Ākāśa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); within <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Tejas</s> (fire); within <s>Tejas</s>, tenfold, <s>Jala</s> (water); and likewise within <s>Jala</s>, tenfold, <s>Pṛthvī</s> (earth) arises. That same earth transforms into the seed in the form of the cosmic egg (<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>).
Within that egg, tenfold, within the envelope of earth, the gross body of <s>Svayambhū</s>, consisting of fourteen worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>), arises by his own will alone.
With that body, <s>Svayambhū</s> is called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
As stated by <s>Manu</s> regarding <s>Svayambhū</s>:
"He, desiring to create various beings from his own body,
first created the waters and cast his seed into them.
That seed became a golden egg, equal in radiance to the thousand-rayed sun.
In it was born <s>Brahmā</s> himself, the grandfather of all worlds.

children.text: sa vai śarīrī prathamaḥ sa vai puruṣa ucyate /
children.translated_text: He was the first embodied being; he is called <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Person).
The primordial creator of beings, <s>Brahmā</s> arose in the beginning.

children.text: āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The waters are called <s>Nārāḥ</s>, for the waters are indeed the offspring of <s>Nara</s> (the cosmic Man).

children.text: tā yadasyāyanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Since they were his first resting place (<s>ayana</s>), he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>."

children.text:
ityādineti |
tata evādipuruṣādvyaṣṭipuruṣāṇāṃ vibhāgāt ante ca tatraiva layāt sa evaika ātmeti śrutismṛtyorvyavahriyate |
tataśca sa nārāyaṇo virāṭśarīrī pṛthivīrūpasvanābhikamalakarṇikāsthānīyasya sumerorupari caturmukhamavāntarabrahmāṇaṃ sṛṣṭvā taddvārānyānapi vyaṣṭiśarīriṇaḥ sthāvarāntān sasarja |
tathā ca smaryate |
children.translated_text:
And so on. Therefore, since individual <s>puruṣas</s> are differentiated from this Primordial Person and at the end dissolve back into him, he alone is referred to as the one <s>Ātman</s> (Self) in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.
Then that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, bearing the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) body, having created the four-faced subsidiary <s>Brahmā</s> upon Mount <s>Sumeru</s> — which occupies the position of the pericarp of the lotus of his own navel, in the form of the earth — through him created other individual embodied beings down to the immobile creatures.
And thus it is recorded in the <s>Smṛti</s>:

children.text:
taccharīrasamutpannaiḥ kāryaistaiḥ karaṇaiḥ saha /
  kṣetrajñāḥ samajāyanta gātrebhyastasya dhīmataḥ // iti /
children.translated_text:
"From his body arose the <s>Kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field, i.e., individual souls),
together with those effects and instruments born of that body, from the limbs of that wise one."

children.text:
yattu śeṣaśāyino nārāyaṇasya nābhikamalaśrotracakṣurādibhyaścaturmukhasyāvirbhāvaḥ śrūyate |
taddainandinasargeṣveva hi kalpabhedena mantavyam |
dainandinapralayeṣveva hi nārāyaṇaśarīre praviśyaikībhūya suptānāṃ devānāṃ caturmukhādikrameṇāvirbhāvaḥ śeṣaśāyinaḥ sakāśād ghaṭate na tvādisargeṣu |
dainandinapralaya eva nārāyaṇasya līlāvigraheṇa śayanāditi |
asyāṃ sṛṣṭau mahattattvasya buddhipūrvakaḥ triguṇātmakaḥ prathamaḥ sargaḥ |
tadanantaraṃ tadupādhikasvayambhuvaḥ sakāśād buddhipūrvakaḥ sargaḥ |
svayambhuvo 'ṅgadevatāḥ svayabhūśca sthūladehanairapekṣyeṇa jñānavattvāt videhā devā ityucyante |
tāsu svayambhūreveśvaraḥ nityeśvarānaṅgīkārāt |
devatāśceśvarakoṭayaḥ avidyānāvṛtopādhikatvāt |
avidyāvṛtopādhikāśca jīvakoṭaya eva |
avidyāvṛtānāvṛtopādhikatve eva jīveśvaravibhājake |
taduktaṃ sa īśo yadvaśe māyā sa jīvo yastayārdita iti |
tadevaṃ sañcaro nirūpitaḥ |
children.translated_text: As for the manifestation of the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>) from the lotus of the navel, ears, eyes, and so forth of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who reclines on <s>Śeṣa</s> — this is to be understood with respect to the daily creations only, differing by <s>kalpa</s>. In the daily dissolutions, the gods who have entered <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s body and become one with it, having slept, manifest in the order beginning with the four-faced one from the one reclining on <s>Śeṣa</s> — but not in the primordial creation. The daily dissolution is [the time] of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s reclining in his sport-form. In this creation, the production of <s>mahat-tattva</s> (the great principle) is preceded by intelligence.

children.text:
tatra yadyasmājjāyate tasyetarāpūraṇenaiva sthitiḥ |
tadvyatirekeṇaiva tatsaṃhāro 'pi tatraiva bhavati |
tathā coktaṃ mahābhārate |
children.translated_text: Therein, whatever arises from something, its continuance is through the filling up of that other. By its opposite, its dissolution too occurs right there. And thus it is said in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:

children.text:
yadyasmājjāyate tattvaṃ tattatra pravilīyate /
  līyante pratilomāni jāyante cottarottaram // iti /
children.translated_text: Whatever principle arises from whatever, it dissolves back into that very thing. They dissolve in reverse order and arise in successive order.

children.text:
ete ca sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārarūpāḥ sthūlā eva pariṇāmāḥ kūṭasthapuruṣavivekāya pradarśitāḥ |
sūkṣmā apyeṣāṃ pariṇāmāḥ smaryante |
yathā
  nityadāhyaṅgabhūtāni bhavanti na bhavanti ca /
  kālenālakṣyavegena sūkṣmatvāttanna dṛśyate // iti /
children.translated_text: These gross transformations in the form of creation, maintenance, and dissolution are demonstrated for the sake of discriminating the immutable <s>Puruṣa</s>. Their subtle transformations too are mentioned, as: "The eternally combustible limbs come into being and cease to be; due to the subtlety of time's imperceptible speed, they are not seen."

children.text:
ata eva sarvaṃ jaḍavastu paramārthataḥ sarvadaiva asaducyate |
tataśca tasmājjaḍavargādvirajyātmaiva paramārthasatyo duḥkhabhīrubhirdraṣṭavyaḥ |
paramārthasatyaṃ ca kūṭasthanityatvam |
tatra kūṭasthanityatvāsaṃhatatvāparārthatvacinmātratvādyasādhāraṇādharmairutkṛṣṭaiḥ prakṛtyādibhyo vivektavyaḥ |
idānīṃ sadevetyādiśrutyartha upapādyate |
pratisañcarānte yannirviśeṣaṃ citsāmānyamavaśiṣyate |
tadeva sadeva saumyedamagra āsīt ekamevādvitīyaṃ brahmetyādiśrutiṣu sadbrahmādipadavācyam |
advitiyatvaṃ tu avaidharmyāvibhāgākhyābhedeneti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, all inert substance is ultimately always called unreal (<s>asat</s>). Hence, from that group of inert [substances], the self alone, being dispassionate, is to be seen as the ultimate truth by those who fear suffering. And ultimate truth is immutable permanence. Therein, the [self] is to be discriminated from <s>Prakṛti</s> and others by its extraordinary properties such as immutable permanence, non-compositeness, non-dependence on another, and being pure consciousness. Now the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> passage "with the gods" (<s>sadeva</s>) is being established. At the end of dissolution, the undifferentiated universal consciousness that remains — that very

children.text: idānīmantakālīnabhagavatsmaraṇasya paramagatihetutvaśravaṇāt tatsmaraṇasya ca sādhyātmasādhibhūtasādhidaivabhagavadanucintanajanyatvādadhyātmādivibhāgaḥ pradarśyate sūtratrayeṇa |
children.translated_text: Now, since it is heard that remembrance of the Lord at the time of death is the cause of the supreme goal, and since that remembrance arises from contemplation of the Lord as the subjective self (<s>sādhyātma</s>), the instrumental self (<s>sādhibhūta</s>), and the presiding deity (<s>sādhidaiva</s>), the division into <s>adhyātma</s> and others is demonstrated by a triad of <s>sūtra</s>s.
And the authority for this is:
"And whoever, at the time of death, remembering Me alone, leaves the body,

children.text: yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ // iti
children.translated_text: he attains My nature — of this there is no doubt." [<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.5]

children.text:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ /
  prayāṇakāle 'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ // iti /
children.translated_text: "Those who know Me together with the <s>adhibhūta</s> and <s>adhidaiva</s>, and together with the <s>adhiyajña</s> — they, with minds disciplined, know Me even at the time of departure." [<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 7.30]
[The subjective self (<s>adhyātma</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_7 ||]
[The objective element (<s>adhibhūta</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_8 ||]
[The presiding deity (<s>adhidaiva</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_9 ||]

children.text:
sūtratrayasyāpi krameṇaiva vyākhyā |
buddhiradhyātmam |
boddhavyamadhibhūtam |
brahmā tatrādhidaivam |
ahaṅkāro 'dhyātmam |
adhimantavyamadhibhūtam |
rudrastatrādhidaivatam |
children.translated_text: The explanation of the three <s>sūtra</s>s is given in order: Intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) is the subjective self (<s>adhyātma</s>). What is to be known is the objective element (<s>adhibhūta</s>). <s>Brahmā</s> is the presiding deity (<s>adhidaiva</s>) therein. Ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) is the subjective self. What is to be conceived is the objective element. <s>Rudra</s> is the presiding deity therein.

children.text:
mano 'dhyātmam |
saṅkalpayitavyamadhibhūtam |
candrastatrādhidaivatam |
śrotramadhyātmam |
śrotavyamadhibhūtam |
diśastatrādhidaivam |
children.translated_text: Mind (<s>manas</s>) is the subjective self. What is to be willed is the objective element. The Moon (<s>Candra</s>) is the presiding deity therein. The ear is the subjective self. What is to be heard is the objective element. The quarters (<s>diśas</s>) are the presiding deity therein.

children.text:
tvagadhyātmam |
sparśayitavyamadhibhūtam |
vāyustatrādhidaivatam /
cakṣuradhyātmam |
draṣṭavyamadhibhūtam |
sūryastatrādhidaivatam |
children.translated_text: Skin is the subjective self. What is to be touched is the objective element. Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) is the presiding deity therein. The eye is the subjective self. What is to be seen is the objective element. The Sun (<s>Sūrya</s>) is the presiding deity therein.
The tongue is the subjective self. Taste is the objective element. <s>Varuṇa</s> is the presiding deity therein.
The nose is the subjective self. Smell is the objective element. Earth (<s>Pṛthivī</s>) is the presiding deity therein.
Speech is the subjective self. Utterance is the objective element. Fire (<s>Vahni</s>) is the presiding deity therein.
The hand is the subjective self. What is to be grasped is the objective element. <s>Indra</s> is the presiding deity therein.

children.text:
pādāvadhyātmam |
gantavyamadhibhūtam |
viṣṇustatrādhidaivatam /
pāyuradhyātmam |
utsraṣṭavyamadhibhūtam |
mitrastatrādhidaivatam |
children.translated_text: The feet are the subjective self. What is to be traversed is the objective element. <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the presiding deity therein. The organ of excretion is the subjective self. What is to be excreted is the objective element. <s>Mitra</s> is the presiding deity therein.

children.text:
upasthamadhyātmam |
ānandayitavyamadhibhūtam |
prajāpatistatrādhidaivatamiti trayodaśavidhaṃ tritayamapi |
tatrātmānaṃ saṅghātamadhikṛtya vartate tadadhyātmaṃ trayodaśakaraṇavargaḥ |
bhūtāni adhikṛtya vartate tadadhibhūtaṃ viṣayavargaḥ |
devatāmadhikṛtya vartata ityadhidaivatam karaṇābhimānidevatāvargaḥ etatsahiteśvarānucintitasyāntakālīnabhagavatsmṛtyā paramagatiḥ phalam |
tasmādetattrikamavaśyaṃ jñātavyamiti bhāvaḥ |
sarvatattvānāṃ jñānaphalaṃ coktaṃ pañcaśikhadhṛtavākyena |
children.translated_text: The generative organ is the subjective self. What is to be delighted in is the objective element. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the presiding deity therein — thus there is a thirteen-fold triad. Therein, what pertains to the self, the composite body, is the subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>) — the group of thirteen instruments. What pertains to the elements is the objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>) — the group of objects. What pertains to the deity is the presiding-deity (<s>adhidaiva</s>) — the group of deities presiding over the instruments. When the Lord is contemplated together with these, remembrance of the Lord at the time of death results in the supreme goal.

children.text: tattvāni yo vedayate yathāvad guṇasvarūpāṇyadhidaivataṃ ca /
children.translated_text: One who knows the principles as they truly are, the natures of the <s>guṇa</s>s, and the presiding deities —

children.text: vimuktapāpmā gatadoṣasaṅgho guṇāṃstu bhuṅkte na guṇaiḥ sa bhujyate //
children.translated_text: freed from sin, with defects and associations gone, one enjoys the <s>guṇa</s>s, but is not enjoyed by the <s>guṇa</s>s.

children.text:
tattvānīti tāntrikī saṃjñā |
tadarthaścātmānātmavivekapratiyogyanuyoginastatpadārthāḥ teṣāṃ bhāvastattatpadapravṛttinimittāni puruṣatvaprakṛtitvādīni pañcaviṃśatijātayaḥ dharmadharmyabhedāt vyaktayo 'pi tattvānītyucyante |

children.translated_text: "Knows" (<s>vedayate</s>) means "understands" — this is the meaning.

children.text: guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi tānyeva svarūpāṇi tāttvikarūpāṇi yeṣāṃ tāni guṇasvarūpāṇi adhidaivatañca adhyātmādhibhūtayorupalakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: The <s>guṇa</s>s are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Their own natures (<s>svarūpa</s>) are their essential forms. Those whose [natures] are the true forms of the <s>guṇa</s>s — these are "the natures of the <s>guṇa</s>s." And <s>adhidaiva</s> is an indicator for both <s>adhyātma</s> and <s>adhibhūta</s>.
"Enjoys the <s>guṇa</s>s" means the <s>guṇa</s>s become subject to his will.

children.text: na guṇaiḥ sa bhujyate guṇavaśo na bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Is not enjoyed by the <s>guṇa</s>s" means he does not become subject to the <s>guṇa</s>s — this is the meaning.

"Principles" (<s>tattvāni</s>) is a <s>Tāntrika</s> designation. Its meaning: the objects that are the correlates and counter-correlates of self/non-self discrimination, their natures — the twenty-five categories such as <s>puruṣatva</s> (selfhood) and <s>prakṛtitva</s> (nature-hood) — as causes of the application of those terms, being distinguished as property and property-bearer (<s>dharma-dharmy</s>), the particulars too are called "principles."
Thus ends the first section on Principles (<s>Tattva-pāda</s>).
Now the second section, the Miscellaneous Section (<s>Prakīrṇaka-pāda</s>), begins.

children.text: tatra pañcasroto 'mbuṃ pañcayonyugracakrāṃ pañcaprāṇormiṃ pañcabuddhyādimūlām pañcāvarttāṃ pañcaduḥkhaughavegāṃ pañcāśadbhedāṃ pañcaparvāmadhīma ityādiśrutyarthopapattaye pañcakāni nirūpayati sūtrajātena ||
children.translated_text: Therein, to establish the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> passage beginning "five-streamed water, five-yoked fierce-wheeled, five-<s>prāṇa</s>-waved, five-rooted-in-intellect-etc., five-eddied, five-sorrow-flood-rapid, fifty-branched, five-sectioned" — the groups of five are explained by a collection of <s>sūtra</s>s.
[The five <s>abhibuddhi</s>s (modes of cognition). || <s>Tats</s>_10 ||]

children.text: abhibuddhirabhimāna icchā karttavyatā kriyeti pañcābhibuddhisaṅgitāḥ / tatrābhibuddhirnāma abhimukhī buddhiḥ idamavaśyaṃ karaṇīyamitirūpā buddhivṛttiḥ / abhimānaścāhaṃ karomītivṛttiḥ / icchā vāñchā saṅkalpo mānasī vṛttiḥ / karttavyatā jñānendriyāṇāṃ śabdādiviṣayā vṛttiḥ / kriyā vacanādilakṣaṇā karmendriyāṇāṃ vṛttiriti //
children.translated_text: Determination (<s>abhibuddhi</s>), self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), obligation (<s>kartavyatā</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>) — these are the five <s>abhibuddhi</s>s as enumerated. Among these: <s>abhibuddhi</s> is the cognition directed toward [an object], a mental function of the form "this must certainly be done." Self-conceit is the function "I am doing." Desire is wish, volition, a mental function. Obligation is the function of the knowledge-senses directed toward objects like sound. Action is the function of the action-senses characterized by speaking and the like.
The <s>abhibuddhi</s>s have been explained.
[The five sources of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmayoni</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_11 ||]

children.text: karmajanyāḥ karmajanakāśca dhṛtiḥ śraddhā sukhā 'vividiṣā vividiṣā ceti pañca ||
children.translated_text: Born of <s>karma</s> and generators of <s>karma</s>: steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), happiness (<s>sukhā</s>), non-desire-to-know (<s>avavidiṣā</s>), and desire-to-know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) — these are the five.
One who guards one's stand in speech, action, and intention,
devoted to that, established in that — this indeed is the characteristic of steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>).
Non-envy, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, austerity (<s>tapas</s>),

children.text: dānaṃ pratigraho homaḥ śraddhāyā lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam //
children.translated_text: giving, receiving gifts, oblation — these are remembered as the characteristics of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>).
One who, seeking gain, cultivates learning, <s>karma</s>, and austerities,
always devoted to expiation — this is declared as happiness (<s>sukha</s>).
Non-desire-to-know (<s>avividiṣā</s>) is the activity that obstructs the desire for Vedic knowledge.
Desire-to-know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) is as follows:

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca nityaṃ cedamacetanam /
children.translated_text: Oneness and separateness, permanence, and "this is unconscious,"

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ satkāryamakṣobhyaṃ jñeyā vividiṣā hi sā //
children.translated_text: subtle, the effect pre-exists in the cause, imperturbable — this is to be known as desire-to-know (<s>vividiṣā</s>).
The desire to know, directed toward the self regarding oneness, separateness, and so forth, is <s>vividiṣā</s>.

Among these, four lead to bondage; only <s>vividiṣā</s> leads to liberation, because it arises from <s>karma</s> that destroys the obstacles to knowledge-liberation and because it generates [such karma].
[The five vital airs (<s>vāyu</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_12 ||]
<s>Prāṇa</s> is in the heart, <s>Apāna</s> in the rectum, <s>Vyāna</s> pervades the entire body,
<s>Udāna</s> is in the region of the throat, and <s>Samāna</s> is situated at the navel.

children.text:
ete pañca kriyāśaktimadantaḥkaraṇavṛttibhedā api vāyusamānagatikatvādvāyudevatākatvācca vāyava ityuktam |
prakarṣeṇa ananādgamanāt prāṇa ityucyate |
adho gamanādapānaḥ |

children.translated_text: <s>Vyāna</s> is so called because of the dispersal of the essence of consumed food and because of yawning.
It causes belching, vomiting, and the like — therefore it is called <s>Udāna</s> (the upward breath), and through it chanting is performed.
It carries the essence of digested food equally [throughout the body] — therefore it is called <s>Samāna</s> (the equalizing breath).
Others mentioned in other <s>Tantras</s> — <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkala</s>, <s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> — are to be subsumed within these very [five].

These five, being also modifications of the inner instrument possessing the power of action, are called "vital airs" (<s>vāyu</s>) because they move like wind and because their presiding deity is <s>Vāyu</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> is so called because it moves forth intensely. <s>Apāna</s> is so called because of its downward movement.
Thus the five <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) have been explained.
[The five <s>karmātmans</s> (action-selves). <s>Tats</s>. 13.]

children.text:
vaikārikastaijaso bhūtādiḥ sānumāno niranumānaśceti karmātmānaḥ karmiṇa ityarthaḥ |
tatra vaikārikaḥ śubhakarmakarttā |

children.translated_text: <s>Taijasa</s> is the performer of non-virtuous action.
<s>Bhūtādi</s> is the performer of deluded action.
<s>Sānumāna</s> is the performer of virtuous-deluded action.
<s>Niranumāna</s> is the performer of non-virtuous-deluded action.

<s>Vaikārika</s> (modified), <s>Taijasa</s> (luminous), <s>Bhūtādi</s> (elemental origin), <s>Sānumāna</s> (with inference), and <s>Niranumāna</s> (without inference) — these are the <s>karmātmans</s>, meaning the performers of action.
Among these, <s>Vaikārika</s> is the performer of virtuous action.
Thus the five <s>karmātmans</s> (action-selves) have been explained.

children.text: idānīṃ pañcāśadbhedāṃ pañcaparvāmadhīma iti śrutyarthopapattaye buddheḥ pañcāśatsargān bahubhiḥ sūtrairuddiśati |
children.translated_text: Now, to establish the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> 'we study the fivefold <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) with fifty divisions,' [the author] indicates the fifty creations of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) through many <s>sūtras</s>.
[The fivefold <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). <s>Tats</s>. 14.]

children.text:
anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātiravidyā patañjalyuktā sarvadarśanasampratipannā |
sā ca pañcadhā avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśajanakatvāt kleśā iti yoge paribhāṣitāḥ |
asmitādīnāṃ caturṇāmavidyākāryatvādavidyātvam |
asmitā anātmanyahaṃvṛttiḥ avidyāsmitayorayaṃ bhedaḥ avidyāyāmadhikaraṇamapi pṛthag bhāsate 'smitāyāṃ tvāroparūpatve 'pi nādhikaraṇaṃ bhāsate |
viṣayeṣūtkaṭecchā rāgaḥ |
dveṣaḥ vairabuddhiḥ |
abhiniveśo maraṇatrāsaḥ |
viduṣāmapi svarasavāhī anādimaraṇaduḥkhānubhavajanitavāsanājanyaḥ śrutismṛtipurāṇeṣu ete avidyābhedāstamaādiśabdaiḥ paribhāṣitāḥ |
tamo moho mahāmohastāmisro 'ndhatāmiśraśceti tattannāmakanarakapradatvāttattannāmakāḥ |
te ca viṣayabhedāt dviṣaṣṭibhedāḥ te yathā |
aṣṭaprakṛtiṣu ātmatvāropāt aṣṭabhedaṃ tamaḥ |
devā aṇimādyaṣṭavidhamaiśvaryamāsādya vayamamṛtā ityabhimānino bhavanti so 'yamabhimāno moho 'ṣṭāvidhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The gods, having attained the eightfold sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), conceive 'We are immortal' — this conceit is delusion (<s>moha</s>), which is eightfold.

children.text: dṛṣṭānuśravikeṣu dvādaśasu viṣayeṣu prāpteṣu mukto 'hamiti manyate so 'bhimāno rāgātiśayanimittatvāt mahāmoho daśavidhaḥ |
children.translated_text: When one has obtained the twelve objects, both seen and heard of, one thinks 'I am liberated' — this conceit, because it arises from the excess of <s>rāga</s> (attachment), is great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>), which is tenfold.

children.text: aṇimādyaṣṭaguṇaiśvarye daśavidhaviṣaye ca pratihatasya krodhād yadduḥkhamutpadyate sa tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśavidhaḥ |
children.translated_text: For one obstructed in the eightfold sovereignty of <s>aṇimā</s> and the rest, and in the tenfold objects, the suffering that arises from anger is <s>tāmisra</s> (darkness), which is eighteenfold.

children.text: devā aṇimādyaṣṭakamaiśvaryaṃ śabdādīṃśca daśa viṣayān bhuñjānāḥ kṣayaśaṅkayā 'tra santi satāsa evāṣṭādaśavidho 'ndhatāmiśra iti dviṣaṣṭibhedā pañcaparvā avidyā ||
children.translated_text: The gods, while enjoying the eightfold sovereignty of <s>aṇimā</s> and the rest and the ten objects beginning with sound, out of fear of decay — the dread 'these are [impermanent]' — this is <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness), which is eighteenfold. Thus <s>avidyā</s> with its five branches has sixty-two divisions.

The cognition of the permanent, pure, pleasant, and self in what is impermanent, impure, painful, and non-self — this is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as stated by <s>Patañjali</s> and accepted by all philosophical systems.
It is fivefold: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life). Because they generate afflictions, they are technically termed <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in <s>Yoga</s>.
Since the four beginning with <s>asmitā</s> are effects of <s>avidyā</s>, they share the nature of <s>avidyā</s>.
<s>Asmitā</s> is the 'I'-notion in what is not the self. The distinction between <s>avidyā</s> and <s>asmitā</s> is: in <s>avidyā</s> there is non-discrimination, in <s>asmitā</s> there is misidentification.
<s>Rāga</s> is attachment that follows upon the recollection of pleasure.
<s>Dveṣa</s> is aversion that follows upon the recollection of pain.
<s>Abhiniveśa</s> is the instinctive clinging to life, even in the learned, arising from the impression of death experienced in a previous birth.
[Incapacity is twenty-eightfold. <s>Tats</s>. 15.]
[Contentment is ninefold. <s>Tats</s>. 16.]
[Attainment is eightfold. <s>Tats</s>. 17.]

children.text:
tatrāśaktayaḥ ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ saptadaśa buddhivadhāḥ |
tatrendriyavadhāḥ |
svasvārthakriyā 'kṣamatārūpāḥ phalato buddhereva te |
children.translated_text:
Among these, the incapacities (<s>aśaktis</s>) are: eleven injuries of the sense organs and seventeen injuries of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect).
Among these, the injuries of the sense organs:
These are in the form of inability to perform their respective functions; in terms of result, they belong to <s>buddhi</s> alone.
Deafness, leprosy, blindness, stupidity, loss of smell,
dumbness, lameness, crippledness, impotence, constipation, and bewilderment.

children.text:
saptadaśa buddhereva vadhāḥ tuṣṭisiddhīnāṃ viparyayarūpāḥ |
tatra tuṣṭiviparyayāḥ |
nāsti pradhānamiti jñānamastītyabhidhīyate |
mahattattvaṃ nāstīti jñānamajñānasalilāḥ |
ahaṅkāro nāstīti mohā |
naiva santi pañcatanmātrāṇīti dṛṣṭiradṛṣṭiḥ |
viṣayāṇāmarjjane pravṛttiḥ asutārā |
rakṣaṇe pravṛttirasupārā |
kṣayadoṣamapaśyataḥ pravṛttiḥ asunetrā |
bhoge śaktiḥ asumātrikā |
hiṃsādoṣamapaśyato bhoge pravṛttiḥ anuttamāmbhasikā |
iti tuṣṭiviparyayā navadhā |
siddhiviparyāsād aṣṭau buddhivadhā ucyante |
nānātvamūhamānasyaikatvānusandhānaṃ sutāramucyate |
śabdamātraśravaṇādviparītagrahaṇamasutārā |
yathā nānātmajño mukta iti śrutvā viparītaṃ pratipanno nānātmajño 'hamamukta iti |
adhyayanaśravaṇaniviṣṭasyāpi jaḍatvādasacchāstropahatabuddhitvādvā pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānasiddhirna bhavati tadajñānam |
yadā ādhyātmikena duḥkhena cābhibhūyate tadajñānapramādam |
evamādhibhautikaduḥkhenābhibhūyate tatpramodamānam |
evamādhidaivikaduḥkhenābhibhavaḥ pramuditamiti |

children.translated_text: Lack of certitude regarding the self, even when instructed by a friend, is pointless.

children.text: svadānamanarthakaṃ jñātvā dānapātrasya guruṇi duḥkhe jāte pramodaḥ pramuditā |
children.translated_text: Knowing one's own giving to be pointless, and rejoicing when great suffering befalls the worthy recipient of gifts — this is <s>pramuditā</s> (delight [misplaced]).
Thus the eight reversals of attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) have been explained.
Thus the seventeen injuries of <s>buddhi</s> have been explained.

The seventeen injuries of <s>buddhi</s> itself are in the form of the reversals of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>).
Among these, the reversals of contentment:
'<s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) does not exist' — such knowledge is called <s>asti</s>.
'The <s>Mahat-tattva</s> does not exist' — such knowledge is 'the waters of non-knowledge' (<s>ajñānasalila</s>).
'<s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) does not exist' — this is delusion (<s>moha</s>).
'The five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) do not exist' — this view is <s>adṛṣṭi</s> (non-vision).
Engagement in acquiring sense objects is <s>asutārā</s>.
Engagement in protecting [them] is <s>asupārā</s>.
Engagement of one who does not see the fault of decay is <s>asunetrā</s>.
Capacity for enjoyment is <s>asumātrikā</s>.
Engagement in enjoyment by one who does not see the fault of causing harm is <s>asumārjikā</s>.
Contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is said to be ninefold.
On this, the verse (<s>kārikā</s>):
Four are internal: named <s>Prakṛti</s> (Nature), <s>Upādāna</s> (Means), <s>Kāla</s> (Time), and <s>Bhāgya</s> (Fortune).
Five are external, from the cessation of sense objects. Thus nine contentments are declared.

children.text:
kutaścit sarvākāreṇa pariṇamamānā prakṛtireva jñānaṃ kariṣyatīti śrutvā yā tuṣṭiḥ sā prakṛtyākhyā tasyā asteti saṃjñā |
pravrajyayaiva jñānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti śrutvā pravrajyopādānena yā tuṣṭiḥ sā salilasaṃjñā |
kālenaiva jñānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti śrutvā pravrajyayā bahukālena yā tuṣṭiḥ sā ādyetyucyate |
children.translated_text: Hearing that knowledge will come by time alone — the contentment arising from long duration of renunciation is called <s>ādya</s> ('primordial').

children.text: bhāgyenaiva jñānaṃ bhaviṣyati madālasā bālakānāmiveti kutaścicchrutvā yā tuṣṭiḥ sā vṛṣṭiritisaṃjñā |
children.translated_text: Hearing from somewhere that knowledge will come by fortune alone, as [it came] to <s>Madālasā</s>'s children — the contentment [arising from this] is designated <s>vṛṣṭi</s> ('rain').
These four are the internal [contentments].

children.text: atha bāhyāḥ pañca śabdādiviṣayeṣvarjanarakṣaṇakṣayabhogahiṃsādidoṣadarśanādyā nivṛttituṣṭayastāsvekā tuṣṭiḥ apāramucyate dvitīyā supāraṃ tṛtīyā pāram anuttamāmbhasikā caturthī uttamāmbhaḥ pañcamī iti nava tuṣṭayo vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now the five external ones: contentments of cessation arising from seeing the faults of acquiring, protecting, decaying, enjoying, and harming in relation to sense objects beginning with sound. Among these, the first contentment is called <s>apāra</s>, the second <s>supāra</s>, the third <s>pāra</s>, the fourth <s>anuttamāmbhasikā</s> (supreme water), and the fifth <s>uttamāmbhas</s> (highest water). Thus the nine contentments have been explained.

Hearing that <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), which transforms in every way from some [cause], will itself produce knowledge — the contentment [arising from this] is called <s>Prakṛti</s>, designated as <s>asti</s> ('it exists').
Hearing that knowledge will come from renunciation alone — the contentment arising from the means of renunciation is designated <s>salila</s> ('water').
Now the eight attainments (<s>siddhis</s>).
On this, the verse (<s>kārikā</s>):
Reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), the three removals of suffering, attainment of a friend (<s>suhṛt</s>),
and giving (<s>dāna</s>) — these are the eight attainments (<s>siddhis</s>). The first three are the goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) of attainment.

children.text:
asyārthaḥ |
bhagavatkṛpāvaśādūhanena tarkeṇaiva jñānamutpadyate sā prathamā siddhistāretyucyate |
śabdaśravaṇamātrādeva yad jñānaṃ sā dvitīyā sutārā |
śiṣyabhāvenādhyayanena yad jñānaṃ sā tṛtīyā tāratāreti |
yadādhyātmikaduḥkhasyāpanodakaṃ jñānaṃ sā caturthī pramodeti |
yadādhibhautikaduḥkhāpanodakaṃ jñānaṃ sā pañcamī pramutiteti |
yadādhidaivikaduḥkhanāśakaṃ jñānaṃ sā ṣaṣṭhī pramodamānā |
yat suhṛtsaṃsargitayā jñānaṃ sā saptamī ramyaketi |

children.translated_text: Knowledge [arising] from a teacher satisfied by one's giving — this is the eighth, called <s>sadāmuditā</s> (ever-joyful).

children.text: āsu prathamāstisro duḥkhavighātātmakānāṃ mukhyānāṃ tisḥṇāṃ siddhīnāmaṅkuśa ākarṣakaḥ sādhaka iti yāvat siddhayastvetā eva |
children.translated_text: Among these, the first three are the goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) — the stimulator, the accomplisher — of the three principal <s>siddhis</s> that consist in the removal of suffering. These are indeed the [true] attainments.
<s>Aṇimā</s> and the other [yogic powers], however, because they obstruct knowledge, are actually non-attainments — this is the teacher's intent.
Thus the eight attainments have been explained.

The meaning of this:
By the grace of the Lord, knowledge arises through reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), i.e., inference alone — this is the first <s>siddhi</s>, called <s>tārā</s>.
Knowledge arising merely from hearing verbal instruction — this is the second, <s>sutārā</s>.
Knowledge arising through study as a disciple — this is the third, <s>tāratārā</s>.
Knowledge that removes subjective suffering (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) — this is the fourth, <s>pramoda</s>.
Knowledge that removes physical suffering (<s>ādhibhautika</s>) — this is the fifth, <s>pramudita</s>.
Knowledge that destroys divine suffering (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) — this is the sixth, <s>pramodamānā</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ sāṃkhyaśāstrasya ṣaṣṭitantratvapratipādanāya pañcāśatsu siddhisargeṣu daśānyān pūrayati sūtreṇa |
children.translated_text: Now, to establish the designation 'Sixty-<s>Tantra</s>' of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system, [the author] fills in ten more [categories] to the fifty <s>siddhi</s>-creations by means of a <s>sūtra</s>.
[The ten fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthas</s>). <s>Tats</s>. 18.]
Existence, oneness, purposefulness, otherness, non-agentship,

children.text: yogo viyogo bahavaḥ pumāṃsaḥ sthitiḥ śarīrasya ca śeṣavṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: conjunction, disjunction, multiplicity of <s>puruṣas</s> (selves), the body's persistence, and residual activity.

children.text:
mūlayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayorarthā dharmā mūlikārthāḥ |
tatrāstitvaṃ dvayordharmaḥ ekatvaṃ sargabhedena nānātvābhāvarūpaṃ prakṛteḥ |
arthavattvaṃ puruṣārthatvaṃ puruṣasyaiva |
pārārthyaṃ ca prakṛtereva |
anyatvaṃ jaḍavargād bhinnatvaṃ puruṣasyaiva |
akartṛtā ca puruṣasyaiva |
yogo viyogaśca dvayoḥ |

children.translated_text: Multiplicity belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s> alone.

children.text: jīvanmuktasya saṃskāramātreṇa cakrabhramivaccharīrasya yā sthitiḥ sā śeṣavṛttiḥ puruṣasya |
children.translated_text: The persistence of the body of one who is liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), sustained merely by residual impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>), like the spinning of a [potter's] wheel — this residual activity (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>) belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: iti daśapadārthāḥ pratyayasargākhyāḥ pañcāśat pūrvoktāḥ ete ca daśa mūlikāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus the ten categories called the 'creation of conditions' (<s>pratyayasarga</s>) are the fifty [already] stated, plus these ten fundamental ones.
Thus sixty categories are stated in the Sixty-<s>Tantra</s> (<s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>).

The attributes (<s>dharmas</s>) of the two fundamentals — <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) — are the fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthas</s>).
Among these: existence is a property of both. Oneness — the absence of multiplicity through differentiation of creation — belongs to <s>Prakṛti</s>.
Purposefulness — serving the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s> alone.
Other-directedness (<s>pārārthya</s>) belongs to <s>Prakṛti</s> alone.
Otherness — difference from the insentient class — belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s> alone.
Non-agentship also belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s> alone.
Conjunction and disjunction belong to both.
Now [the author] presents the creation of the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) by means of a <s>sūtra</s>.
[The favoring creation (<s>anugrahasarga</s>). <s>Tats</s>. 19.]

children.text: pañcatanmātrā anugṛhyopādānakāraṇatvena svīkṛtya yaḥ sargaḥ so 'nugrahasargaḥ |
children.translated_text: The creation that proceeds by favoring the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and accepting them as material causes — that is the favoring creation (<s>anugrahasarga</s>).
