children.text: pañcānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sacaturmukhasanakādīnāṃ svasya līlāvigrahe sargo bhaktānamanugrahārthaṃ so 'pyanugrahasargaḥ pañcatanmātrebhya eva ||
children.translated_text: The creation of the five <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] and <s>Sanaka</s> and others — in his own playful form (<s>līlāvigraha</s>) for the purpose of bestowing grace upon devotees — that too is a grace-creation (<s>anugrahasarga</s>), arising from the five <s>tanmātras</s> alone.
Now he describes the elemental creation (<s>bhūtasarga</s>).
[The elemental creation is of fourteen kinds. || Tats_20 ||]

children.text:
brāhmaprājāpatyasaumyaindragāndharvayakṣarākṣasapaiśācā ityaṣṭau devasargāḥ |
paśupakṣimṛgasarīsṛpasthāvarā iti pañcavidhāstairyagyonayaḥ |
mānuṣaścaikavidho brāhmaṇādiścaṇḍālānta iti |
gavādimūṣakāntāḥ paśavaḥ |
garuḍādimaśakāntāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ |
siṃhādiśṛgālāntā mṛgāḥ |
śeṣādidundubhāntāḥ sarīsṛpāḥ |
parvatāditṛṇāntāḥ sthāvarā iti |
children.translated_text:
The <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s> — these are the eight divine creations.
Animals (<s>paśu</s>), birds (<s>pakṣi</s>), wild animals (<s>mṛga</s>), reptiles (<s>sarīsṛpa</s>), and immobile beings (<s>sthāvara</s>) — these are the five types of animal births.
The human is of one kind, from <s>brāhmaṇa</s> down to <s>caṇḍāla</s>.
Animals range from cows to mice.
Birds range from <s>Garuḍa</s> to mosquitoes.
Wild animals range from lions to jackals.
Reptiles range from <s>Śeṣa</s> to earthworms.
Immobile beings range from mountains to grasses.

children.text:
atra kārikā |
  aṣṭavidho daivastairyagyona(ya)śca pañcadhā bhavati /
  mānuṣaścaikavidhaḥ samasato bhautikaḥ sargaḥ // iti /
  etatsaṃsāramaṇḍalam anyānapyanuktān sargānuddiśati sūtratrayeṇa /
children.translated_text:
Here is the verse:
"The divine creation is eightfold; the animal creation is fivefold;
the human is of one kind. In sum, this is the elemental creation."
To indicate other creations not yet mentioned within this wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), three <s>sūtras</s> are presented.
[Threefold bondage. || Tats_21 ||]
[Threefold liberation. || Tats_22 ||]
[Threefold valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). || Tats_23 ||]

children.text:
prākṛtiko vaikṛtiko dākṣiṇa iti trayo bandhāḥ |
prākṛto 'ṣṭaprakṛtiṣvabhimānarūpaḥ |
dvitīyastu pravrajitānāmapi śabdādiṣu manasaḥ saṅgaḥ |
tṛtīyastu gṛhasthādīnāṃ kāmopahatacetasāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadatāṃ dakṣiṇābandhaḥ |
children.translated_text:
Natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>), modified (<s>vaikṛtika</s>), and sacrificial-gift (<s>dākṣiṇa</s>) — these are the three types of bondage.
The natural bondage is in the form of identification with the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (original principles).
The second is the attachment of the mind to objects like sound, even for renunciants.
The third is the bondage of sacrificial gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) for householders and others whose minds are afflicted by desire, who give gifts.
And this has been stated by the teacher <s>Pañcaśikha</s>:

children.text: prākṛtena tu bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca /
children.translated_text: "By the natural bondage, and likewise by the modified,
and by the third, the bondage of sacrificial gifts, the bound creature revolves."
The threefold nature of liberation has also been stated:

children.text: ādau tu mokṣo jñānena dvitīyo rāgasaṃkṣayāt /
children.translated_text: "The first liberation is through knowledge; the second through the destruction of passion;
the third through the cessation of affliction — thus the characteristic of liberation is explained."

children.text:
jñānodrekādavidyānivṛttirūpa ekaḥ rāgasaṃkṣayādindriyopaśamarūpo dvitīyaḥ kṛcchrakṣayāddharmādharmakaraṇarūpāddharmādharmānutpādarūpastṛtīyaḥ |
etattrayaṃ jñānadvārabhūtatvād gauṇaṃ mokṣatrayam |
ātyantikatrividhaduḥkhanivṛttireva mukhyo mokṣaḥ |
taduktaṃ gotamena sūtreṇa duḥkhajanmapravṛttidoṣamithyājñānānāmuttarottarāpāye tadanantarābhāvādapavarga iti /
children.translated_text:
The first is in the form of the cessation of ignorance through the preponderance of knowledge. The second is in the form of the pacification of the senses through the destruction of passion and the like. The third arises from the cessation of the practice of merit and demerit, in the form of the non-arising of merit and demerit.
These three are secondary forms of liberation, since they serve as gateways to knowledge.
The primary liberation is the absolute cessation of the threefold suffering.
As stated by <s>Gotama</s> in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Through the successive removal of suffering, birth, activity, defects, and false knowledge, the one immediately following ceases, and this is <s>apavarga</s> (final release).'

children.text:
uktānāṃ padārthānāṃ siddhyarthaṃ pramāṇānyāha mānādhīnatvānmeyasiddheḥ |
trividhaṃ pramāṇamiti |
pratyakṣānumānaśabdā iti |
tatrānadhigatayathārthajñānaṃ pramā tatkaraṇaṃ pramāṇamiti sāmānyalakṣaṇamekam |
arthākārānadhigatayathārthāntaḥkaraṇavṛttiriti dvitīyam |
tatra pratyakṣamindriyajanyamanadhigatayathārthajñānaṃ pratyakṣapramā |
tatkaraṇaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇam |
indriyajanyānadhigatayathārthāntaḥkaraṇavṛttiriti dvitīyam |
yathārthaliṅgajñānājjāyamānaṃ jñānamanumitistatkaraṇamanumānamityekam |
liṅgajñānājjāyamānā sādhyaviśiṣṭapakṣākārāntaḥkaraṇavṛttiriti dvitīyam |
āptavacanajanyajñānaṃ śabdapramā tatkaraṇaṃ śabdapramāṇamityekaṃ lakṣaṇam |
āptavacanajanyā padārthāsaṃsargākārāntaḥkaraṇavṛttiriti dvitīyaṃ śabdapramāṇalakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text:
For the establishment of the categories described, he presents the means of valid knowledge, since the establishment of what is to be known depends on the means of knowing.
'Threefold valid knowledge' — namely, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>).
Therein, the general definition is: <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is true knowledge of what has not been previously known; <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is its instrument.
The second [definition]: a mental modification (<s>antaḥkaraṇavṛtti</s>) that is true and previously unacquired, in the form of the object.
Therein, perceptual valid cognition is true, previously unacquired knowledge born of the senses.
Its instrument is the perceptual means of knowledge.
The second [definition]: a mental modification born of the senses, true and previously unacquired.
Knowledge arising from the cognition of a valid inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is inferential cognition; its instrument is inference — this is one [definition].
The second: a mental modification in the form of the subject qualified by the probandum, arising from the cognition of the inferential mark.
Knowledge born from the words of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is verbal valid cognition; its instrument is the verbal means of knowledge — this is one definition.
The second definition of verbal means of knowledge: a mental modification in the form of the relation of word-meanings, born from the words of a trustworthy person.
A trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is one who is engaged in his own work, free from passion and aversion, possessing knowledge, and endowed with good character.

children.text: idaṃ tu jñānopadeṣṭurevāptalakṣaṇam vastuto yathābhūtārthasyopadeṣṭā puruṣa ityeva /|
children.translated_text: But this is the definition of a trustworthy person only as an instructor of knowledge. In reality, a person who teaches things as they truly are — that is the [definition].

children.text:
uktapadārtheṣu kecitpratyakṣasiddhāḥ kecitanumānasiddhāḥ |
ubhābhyāṃ yanna siddhaṃ tacchabdapramāṇena sidhyati yathendro devānāṃ rājā uttarāḥ kuravaḥ sauvarṇo meruḥ svarge 'psarasaḥ ete padārthā na pratyakṣānumānagamyāḥ kintu śabdaikagamyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Among the categories described, some are established through perception, some through inference. What is not established by both of these is established through verbal testimony — for example, '<s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods,' '<s>Uttarakuru</s> (the northern continent),' 'Mount <s>Meru</s> is golden,' 'in heaven there are <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs).' These entities are not knowable through perception or inference, but are knowable through verbal testimony alone.

children.text: antaḥkaraṇasyendriyāṇāṃ cāvibhaktaḥ saṅkocavikāsaśālyagrabhāgo vṛttirabhyupeyate bhāgaguṇābhyāṃ tattvāntaraṃ vṛttiḥ sambandhārthaṃ sarpatīti sāṃkhyapravacanasūtrāt |
children.translated_text: The undivided tip of the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) and the senses, which possesses the capacity for contraction and expansion, is accepted as the <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification). 'The <s>vṛtti</s>, being a different principle from [its source] by portion and by quality, creeps forth for the purpose of connection' — from the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana Sūtra</s>.
'Portion' means a separated part; 'by quality' too it is a different principle, a different entity — meaning an undivided part.

children.text: tathā cāntaḥkaraṇavṛttirindriyavṛttidvārārthasannikṛṣṭā bhavati tata indriyavṛttyā sahārthākārā pariṇamate sā cārthākārā vṛttirguṇarūpā sarvātmanāṃ vibhutve 'pi svasvāminyevātmani pratibimbate nānyatra abādisvasvāmibhāvasya pratibimbaniyāmakatvāt anyathā 'tiprasaṅgāt pratibimbaścādhiṣṭhānagatāyā buddhervikāraḥ pariṇāmaḥ svattvaṃ ca svāmiprakāśitavṛttijanyasaṃskāravattvam |
children.translated_text: Thus the modification of the inner instrument, through the modification of the senses, comes into contact with the object. Then it transforms together with the sense-modification into the form of the object. That <s>vṛtti</s> in the form of the object, being of the nature of a <s>guṇa</s> (quality), though all souls are all-pervading, is reflected only in its own master, the soul — not elsewhere, because the master-servant relationship to the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is the determining factor for reflection; otherwise there would be an infinite regress. And the reflection is a modification, a transformation, of the <s>buddhi</s> residing in the substratum. 'Ownership' means possessing impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born of the <s>vṛtti</s> illuminated by the owner.

children.text: svāmitvaṃ ca svaniṣṭhasaṃskārajanakavṛttiprakāśakatvaṃ sā ca vṛttirātmani sthitā satī arthākārā ātmākārā ca svasamānākāraṃ pariṇāmāntaraṃ dhatte sa evātmani vṛttipratibimbo viṣayatākhyaḥ sambandha iti tadavacchinnaṃ caitanyaṃ pratyakṣapramā ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmītyākārārthātmaviṣayiṇī taduktam //
children.translated_text: 'Mastership' means the capacity to illuminate the <s>vṛtti</s> that generates impressions residing in oneself. That <s>vṛtti</s>, situated in the self, being in the form of the object and in the form of the self, produces another transformation of the same form — that is the reflection of the <s>vṛtti</s> in the self, called 'objecthood' (<s>viṣayatā</s>), which is the relation. The consciousness delimited by that [reflection] is perceptual valid cognition, of the form 'I know the pot' — having object, self, and subject as its content. As stated:
And here is the process of knowledge:
"Just as <s>Rāhu</s>, though invisible, is seen through the eclipsed moon,
so the self, whose nature is mere experience, is perceived through the visible [object]."

children.text: iyaṃ ca pratyakṣā vṛttirviṣayadeśe jāyamānā tatraivātmani pratibimbate ātmano vibhutvāt yatra cendriyadvāraṃ vinā manaḥ svavāsanāvaśādyatrārthena sambaddhyate tatra tadākārā vṛttirmānasaṃ pratyakṣam |
children.translated_text: This perceptual <s>vṛtti</s>, arising in the region of the object, is reflected in the self right there, because the self is all-pervading. And where the mind, without the door of the senses, by the force of its own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), is connected with an object — there the <s>vṛtti</s> in the form of that [object] is mental perception (<s>mānasa pratyakṣa</s>).
And it has been stated:
"Abandoning the resting-place of the body, wherever the bird of the mind
goes by the force of its own latent impressions, there the self is experienced."
"Through the visible" means through the <s>vṛtti</s>.
Thus in the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>.
Thus the process of perception.

Likewise, a <s>vṛtti</s> in the form of the subject qualified by the probandum, born from valid cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), is the means of inference. The consciousness delimited by its reflection is inferential cognition.
Thus the process of inference.

children.text: yathārthapadasmṛtijanyā padārthasaṃsargākārā vṛttiḥ śabdapramāṇam tatpratibimbāvacchinnacaitanyaṃ śābdī pramā idaṃ pramāṇadvayamāntarameva |

aparokṣatvaṃ parokṣatvaṃ smṛtitvaṃ saṃśayatvaṃ viparyayatvaṃ pramātvamapramātvaṃ ca sarve vṛttidharmā eva tatpratibimbavaśāccaitanye 'pyupacaryante tatrāparokṣatvaparokṣatvasmṛtitvāni jātayaḥ saṃśayaśca bhāsamānavirodhobhayakoṭispṛgvṛttiḥ |
children.translated_text: Immediacy (<s>aparokṣatva</s>), mediacy (<s>parokṣatva</s>), being a memory (<s>smṛtitva</s>), being a doubt (<s>saṃśayatva</s>), being an error (<s>viparyayatva</s>), being valid (<s>pramātva</s>), and being invalid (<s>apramātva</s>) — all these are properties of the <s>vṛtti</s> alone, and through its reflection they are figuratively attributed to consciousness as well. Among these, immediacy, mediacy, and being a memory are kinds. And doubt is a <s>vṛtti</s> that touches both alternatives of an appearing contradiction.

children.text: yatra yannāsti tatra tanniścayo viparyayaḥ yathārthavṛttiḥ pramā ayathārthavṛtirapramā atra pramātrādivibhāgaviṣaye vijñānācāryāṇāṃ kārikā |
children.translated_text: Where what is not present is determined to be present — that is error (<s>viparyaya</s>). A <s>vṛtti</s> conforming to reality is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>); a <s>vṛtti</s> not conforming to reality is invalid cognition (<s>apramā</s>). Regarding the division of the knower and others, here is a verse by the <s>Vijñānācāryas</s> (masters of knowledge):

children.text: pramātā cetanaḥ śuddhaḥ pramāṇaṃ vṛttireva ca /
children.translated_text: "The knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) is pure consciousness; the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is the <s>vṛtti</s> itself;
valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is the reflection of object-formed <s>vṛttis</s> in consciousness.

A <s>vṛtti</s> in the form of the relation of word-meanings, born from the recollection of the true meanings of words, is the verbal means of knowledge. The consciousness delimited by its reflection is verbal valid cognition. These two means of knowledge are internal only.
The object of the reflected <s>vṛttis</s> is called the knowable (<s>meya</s>).
The <s>vṛttis</s> are witnessed by the witness-self (<s>sākṣin</s>), because they do not depend on an instrument.
And the nature of witness-hood is direct seeing — as stated in the <s>Sāṃkhya Sūtra</s>."

children.text: jñānasya ca janyatvaṃ vināśitvamātmadharmatvaṃ ca pratibimbāvacchinnatvenopapādanīyam ātmarūpasya jñānasya nityatvāt |
viśiṣṭe hi vidhiniṣedhau viśeṣaṇamupasaṃkrāmataḥ sati viśeṣye bādha iti nyāyāt |
children.translated_text: For regarding a qualified [entity], positive and negative injunctions apply to the qualifier, while the qualified itself is sublated — according to this principle.

children.text: ādhārādheyabhāvo 'pi khe khagodaya itivadupapādanīyaḥ vṛttīnāmātmani pratibimbe pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: Even the relation of support and supported is to be explained like the rising of a bird in the sky. The proof for the reflection of <s>vṛttis</s> in the self:
"In that spacious mirror [of the self],
all perceptions of objects are reflected, like trees on the bank in a lake."

The produced nature, perishable nature, and being a property of the self that knowledge has — these are to be explained through the delimitation by the reflection, since knowledge in its essential nature as the self is eternal.
Thus in the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>.
Thus, in brief, the process of knowledge.

children.text:
atra śāstre 'nuktāḥ svāvirodhinaḥ śāstrāntarīyā api padārthāḥ grāhyāḥ sārādānaṃ ṣaṭpadavaditi sāṃkhyapravacanasūtrāt |
sarvataḥ sāramādadyāt puṣpebhya iva ṣaṭpada iti smṛteśca |
ete ca prakṛtyādayaḥ padārthāḥ saṃhatatvapadārthatvajaḍatvapratikṣaṇapariṇāmitvādidoṣairduṣṭatvāddheyāstebhyo 'pyadhikaṃ heyamāha |
children.translated_text:
Categories from other <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) that are not mentioned in this <s>śāstra</s> but are not contradictory to it should also be accepted — from the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana Sūtra</s>: 'One should extract the essence, like a bee [from flowers].' And from the <s>Smṛti</s>: 'One should gather the essence from everywhere, like a bee from flowers.'
These categories beginning with <s>Prakṛti</s>, being afflicted by defects such as compositeness, being objects, being insentient, and undergoing momentary transformation, are to be rejected. And even more to be rejected than these, he declares:
[Threefold suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). || Tats_24 ||]

children.text:
ādhyātmikāmadhibhautikamādhidaivikaṃ ceti |
tatrādhyātmikaṃ dvividhaṃ śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ca |
tatra śārīraṃ vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ vaiṣamyeṇotpannaṃ jvarātisārādi |
kāmakrodhalobhādijanyaṃ mānasaṃ mānuṣamṛgasarpādijanyamādhibhautikaṃ śītoṣṇavātavṛṣṭijanyamādhidaivikam |
anena trividhaduḥkhenābhibhūtasya tarati śokamātmaviditi śrutvā ātmani jijñāsā jāyate |
yathā tṛṣitasya pānīyapipāsā |
children.translated_text: [suffering is] of three kinds: pertaining to the self (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), pertaining to beings (<s>ādhibhautika</s>), and pertaining to the gods (<s>ādhidaivika</s>). Among these, the suffering pertaining to the self is of two kinds: bodily and mental. The bodily kind is produced by the imbalance of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), such as fever, diarrhea, and the like. The mental kind, produced by desire, anger, greed, and others, is [caused by] humans, animals,
[The author] shows the connection of the previously done exposition of the <s>tattvas</s> with the goal of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).

children.text: [etatparaṃ yāthārthyaṃ etajjñātvā kṛtakṛtyaḥ syānna punastrividhaduḥkhenābhibhūyate || Tats_25 ||]
children.translated_text: ['This supreme truth — having known it, one becomes accomplished and is no longer overwhelmed by the threefold suffering.' <s>Tattva-sūtra</s> 25.]

children.text:
etadyāthārthyaṃ paraṃ śāstrāntaroktādyāthārthyādutkṛṣṭaṃ nyāyavaiśeṣikoktayāthārthyasyāṣṭaprakṛtyakathanādapūrṇatvam idaṃ tu tatkathanena pūrṇaṃ śrutisammatatvācca paraṃ sarvotkṛṣṭamityarthaḥ |
śrutiśca gopālatāpanīye ekamevādvitīyaṃ brahmāsīt tasmādavyaktādavyaktamevākṣaraṃ tasmānmahanmahato 'haṅkārastataḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi tebhyo bhūtāni iti spaṣṭameva sāṃkhyayogoktamahadādikrameṇa sṛṣṭiḥ śrūyata iti |
etajjñātvā ātmānātmavivekasākṣātkāradvārā kṛtakṛtyaḥ syānniṣprayojanaḥ syādityarthaḥ |
kiṃ punastatprayojanaṃ tatrāha |
na punastrividhaduḥkhenābhibhūyata iti |
pūrvoktatrividhaduḥkhena na yujyate duḥkhātyantanivṛttirūpo mokṣo bhavatītyarthaḥ |
nanu duḥkhaṃ tāvat trividham anāgataṃ vartamānamatītaṃ ceti |
sāṃkhyayogavedāntānāṃ satkāryavādāśrayaṇāt sarvameva kāryamavasthātrayeṇa nityam |
anāgato ghaṭo varttamāno ghaṭo 'tīto ghaṭa ityavasthātraye 'pi ghaṭasyāvasthādharmiṇo 'nugatapratyayāt |
prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsayoścānaṅgīkārāt |
na ca tatkāle kathamabhāvapratyaya iti vācyam varttamānapratiyogikasāmayikātyantābhāvenaiva tadupapatteriti |
evaṃ cānagatātītaduḥkhayorabhāve 'pi na puruṣārthaḥ bhogyaduḥkhābhāvasyaiva puruṣārthatvāt |
vartamānaduḥkhaṃ ca bhogyamapi bhogenaiva naṅkṣyatīti tadabhāvo na puruṣārthaḥ puruṣaprayatnanirapekṣatvāt puruṣaprayatnasāpekṣasyaiva puruṣārthatvāt tathā ca kathaṃ duḥkhābhāvasya bhogyahetutayā tadabhāvasya ca puruṣakṛtisādhyatayā puruṣārthatvaṃ duḥkhahetūcchede puruṣavyāparāt prāyaścittavaditi |
taduktaṃ patañjalinā |
heyaṃ duḥkhamanāgataṃ vivekakhyātiravitpravā hānopāya iti sūtradvayena /
children.translated_text: This truth (<s>yāthārthya</s>) is supreme — superior to the truth stated in other <s>śāstras</s>. The truth stated by <s>Nyāya</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> is incomplete because it does not describe the eight <s>prakṛtis</s>; but this [Sāṃkhya truth], by describing them, is complete, and because it is approved by <s>śruti</s> (Vedic revelation), it is supreme, i.e., most excellent — this is the meaning. The <s>śruti</s>

children.text:
sāṃkhyānāṃ ca sarvātmanāmavaidharmyābheda eva tattvamasivākyārtho nāvibhāgādiḥ tajjñānasyaivābhimānanivarttakatvāt |
tadvākyasya ca śvetaketoranūcānatvādyabhimānanivṛttyarthameva pravṛtteḥ tathā ca layāvaśiṣṭacitsāmānyaṃ tatpadārthaḥ taduktaṃ vijñānācāryavaryairasmadgurubhirbhāṣyādyaślokena /
  eko 'dvitīya iti vedavacāṃsi puṃsi sarvābhimānavinivartanato 'sya muktyai /
  vaidharmyalakṣaṇabhidā virahaṃ vadanti nākhaṇḍatāṃ kha iva dharmaśatāvirodhāt // iti /
children.translated_text: And for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, the meaning of the statement 'That thou art' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>) is precisely the non-difference through non-dissimilarity of all selves — not non-distinction, etc. — because only that knowledge removes the [false] sense of ego-identity. And because that statement was directed toward <s>Śvetaketu</s> for the purpose of removing the pride of being learned and so forth,

children.text:
tathā caprakṛtyādiviviktasarvātmanāmavaidharmyabhedasākṣātkārāt kartṛtvādyabhimānanivṛttau tatkāryarāgadveṣadharmādyanutpādāt pūrvotpannakarmaṇāṃ cāvidyārāgādisahakāryucchedena janmādyanārambhakatvādbhogena prārabdhasamāptyanantaraṃ punarjanmābhāvena bhogāpavargasamāptyā cāntaḥkaraṇasya nāśenaiva trividhaduḥkhātyantanivṛttirūpo mokṣo bhavatīti paramakṛtakṛtyatā |
idaṃ cātrāvadheyam |
gurūpadeśaśāstrābhyāmutpannamapi jñānamaparokṣatvāyābhyasanīyameva |

children.translated_text: Without that [direct realization], the removal of non-mediate ignorance is impossible.

children.text: aparokṣyabhrame hi samānaviśeṣyakā 'parokṣyaviparītaniścayasyaiva nivartakatvāvadhāraṇāt taduktaṃ vāsiṣṭhe |
children.translated_text: For in the case of non-mediate error, it is ascertained that only a non-mediate cognition having the same qualificand is capable of removing [it]. Thus it is said in the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>:
Even by one who has known the truth, this [practice of] 'not this' must be constantly repeated,
for the clearing-nut by name alone does not purify water.

And thus, from the direct realization of the non-difference through non-dissimilarity of all selves distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest, when the false identification with agency and the like ceases, and when the effects thereof — attachment, aversion, merit, and the rest — no longer arise, and when the cooperation of ignorance, attachment, and the rest with previously accumulated <s>karmas</s> is cut off, those [karmas] become incapable of initiating birth, etc.

children.text:
antardhvāntavināśāya śābdabodho na hi kṣamaḥ /
  na naśyati tamo rāma kṛtayā dīpavārtayā // iti /
children.translated_text: Verbal knowledge is not capable of destroying the inner darkness; darkness, O <s>Rāma</s>, does not perish merely by talking about a lamp.

children.text:
evamabhyāsāt komalakaṇṭakanyāyena jñāne jāte yogarūḍha ityucyate yogī asmāt pūrvastu yuñjānaḥ tataḥ paramahaṃsāśrameṇa vikṣepakāṇi karmāṇi tyaktvā jñānaniṣṭhāparyantamabhyaset |
savāsanāvidyocchedo jñānaniṣṭhā |
tataḥ sa yukto jīvanmukto guṇātīta iti cocyate |
children.translated_text: Then he is called a liberated-while-living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), united [with truth], and beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>guṇātīta</s>).
Being devoid of identification with the <s>guṇas</s> is itself the state of being beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, and is the defining characteristic of one liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>).
[For whom] neither does [something] arise nor set — neither pleasure nor pain [affect] the radiance of [their] face;
one whose condition remains as before — that person is called <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living).

Thus through repeated practice, by the maxim of the tender thorn, when knowledge arises, one is called a <s>yogin</s> 'established in <s>yoga</s>' (<s>yogarūḍha</s>). Before that, one is [called] 'striving' (<s>yuñjāna</s>). Then, having renounced through the state of a supreme renunciant (<s>paramahaṃsa-āśrama</s>) all <s>karmas</s> that cause distraction, one should practice until the culmination of steadfastness in knowledge. The eradication of ignorance along with its latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) through knowledge
Even while acting in accordance with passion, aversion, fear, and the like,
one who is internally clear like the sky — that person is called <s>jīvanmukta</s>.
This alone is the mark of one whose formless form has been stilled from the long delusion of <s>saṃsāra</s> and who has found peace:
that in the knower of That, desire, anger, despondency, delusion, greed, and calamities become subtler day by day.

children.text: anyaccātra sāṃkhyavidyāyāṃ bhagavadbhakterevāsādhāraṇakāraṇatvaṃ jñeyam anyathā devakṛtavighnairyogadhvaṃso bhavatyeva yathoktaṃ bhāgavate |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in this <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge, devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to the Lord (<s>Bhagavat</s>) should be understood as the unique cause. Otherwise, yoga is surely destroyed by obstacles created by the gods. As stated in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>:
O Lotus-eyed One, those others who consider themselves liberated but whose intellects are impure due to the absence of devotion to You,

children.text: āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṃ padaṃ tataḥ patantyadho 'nādṛtayuṣmadaṅdhrayaḥ //
children.translated_text: having ascended with great difficulty to the supreme state, fall down from there because they have not honored Your feet.

children.text:
śreyaḥśrutiṃ bhaktimudasya te vibho kliśyanti ye kevalabodhalabdhaye /
  teṣāmasau kleśala eva śiṣyate nānyadyathā sthūlatuṣāvaghātinām // iti /
children.translated_text: Those who, setting aside devotion — the path to the highest good that is proclaimed in <s>śruti</s> — undergo suffering merely for the sake of obtaining knowledge alone, O Lord — for them that [path] remains only a source of suffering, like those who thresh mere husks.

children.text: idānīṃtanāḥ kecana vaiṣṇavā etādṛśavākyairbhagavadbhaktiṃ puraskṛtya sāmānyato jñānamārgaṃ khaṇḍayati te tu vidyāvivekānabhijñāḥ sthūlamataya eva |
children.translated_text: Certain modern <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, foregrounding devotion to the Lord on the basis of such statements, generally reject the path of knowledge. But they are merely ignorant of the distinction of [types of] knowledge, being of coarse understanding.
And in the <s>Nāradīya</s> [Purāṇa], in the section on <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge:
When firm devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the activator of <s>māyā</s>, is established in humans,
He easily reveals to them their own Self as distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s>, like a lamp.

children.text: citte hi svavaśe yogaḥ siddhyet tattu jagatpatim /
children.translated_text: Yoga succeeds when the mind is under one's control; but who,
without taking refuge in the Lord of the world, can restrain [the mind which is] unmanifest and exceedingly restless?

children.text:
tasmānmumukṣoḥ susukho mārgaḥ śrīviṣṇusaṃśrayaḥ /
  cittena cintayānena vañcyate dhruvamanyathā // iti /
gītāyāṃ caturdaśādhyāye /
  māṃ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate /
  sa guṇān samatītyaiva brahmabhūyāya kalpyate // iti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for one seeking liberation, the most easy path is taking refuge in Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>; otherwise one is surely deceived by a brooding mind. And in the <s>Gītā</s>, in the fourteenth chapter: 'And one who serves Me with unwavering <s>bhakti-yoga</s> transcends these <s>guṇas</s>

children.text: brahmabhūyāya pūrṇatvenābhivyaktaye guṇābhidhānaṃ tattadavacchinnatvenaivābhivyajyate tasmād bhagavadbhaktireva mukhyaṃ sādhanaṃ sāṃkhyayogavidyāyāmiti siddham |
children.translated_text: For the manifestation of becoming <s>Brahman</s> in its fullness, the designation of the <s>guṇas</s> is manifested only as delimited by each [guṇa]; therefore, devotion to the Lord (<s>bhagavad-bhakti</s>) alone is the primary means in the knowledge of <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s> — this is established.
This <s>Tattvayāthārthyadīpana</s> (Lamp on the True Nature of Reality) has been composed for the benefit of others.

children.text: tena me prīyatāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ paramātmā jagadguruḥ //
children.translated_text: May <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātmā</s>), the Teacher of the world (<s>Jagadguru</s>), be pleased by it.
Because of His independence, He alone — the cowherd boy (<s>Gopāla-bālaka</s>) — is the sole agent;
I am like a wooden puppet, and He, named <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, is the Great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>).
For those desiring to know the meaning of the <s>Purāṇas</s>, *** this has been composed by me.

children.text: tebhyaṃ samarpitaṃ caitat tenāpi prīyatāṃ hariḥ //
children.translated_text: And this has been offered to them; may <s>Hari</s> be pleased by it as well.
Thus the <s>Tattvayāthārthyadīpana</s>, composed by <s>Bhāvāgaṇeśa</s>, son of <s>Bhāvā Viśvanātha Dīkṣita</s>, is completed.
